He sees that Allah's commands and decrees constantly descend to the farthest reaches of various worlds, through which He manages and disposes of all affairs, giving life and causing death, honoring and humiliating, lowering and raising, giving and depriving, averting calamities and sending them, changing the conditions of people, and singly managing His dominion, over which no one besides Him has any authority, in many other ways. As for His decrees, in accordance with His will, they find their way to everything, for Allah the Most High said: 'He arranges [each] matter from the heaven to the earth; then it will ascend to Him in a Day, the extent of which is a thousand years of those which you count.' (As-Sajdah, 5). For one whose knowledge and worship fully conform to what has been mentioned above, his Lord alone suffices him. The same applies to one who testifies to Allah's all-encompassing knowledge, His hearing, sight, life, eternal existence, and other attributes. However, the ability for such testimony has been granted only to the close ones among those who excelled in faith.
short_answer: Learn, understand the meanings, supplicate with them, and live by them.

question: What is the opposite of recognizing Allah as the sole possessor of the aforementioned names and attributes?
answer: The opposite of this is all kinds of deviations (Ilhad) concerning Allah's names, attributes, and signs. Such deviations are of three types: 1 - The deviation of the polytheists, who denied the true meaning of the names of Allah the Most High and applied these names to idols, adding to them, subtracting from them, and forming names like Al-Lat from Al-Ilah (the Deity), Al-'Uzza from Al-'Aziz (the Almighty), and Manat from Al-Mannan (the Bestower of Favors). 2 - The deviation of the anthropomorphists (Mushabbihah), who gave their explanations of how Allah's attributes should be interpreted and likened them to human attributes. This type of deviation is similar to that of the polytheists, for while the latter equated creation with the Lord of the worlds, the former degraded Him to the level of created forms, likening the Most High and Holy to these forms. 3 - The deviation of the negators (Mu'attilah), who denied Allah's attributes and were divided into two groups: Some of them recognized the names of the Most High but denied the attributes of perfection which these names encompass. They said: 'The Most Merciful and the Especially Merciful without mercy, the Knowing without knowledge, the Hearing without hearing, the Seeing without sight, the Powerful without power,' etc. Others openly and completely denied both the names themselves and their content, describing Allah as absolute non-existence, having neither names nor attributes. Exalted is Allah! He is far above the statements of the wrongdoers, the deniers, and the deviators, for Allah the Most High said: '[He is] Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, so worship Him and have patience for His worship. Do you know of any similarity to Him?' (Maryam, 65). 'There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing.' (Ash-Shura, 11). Allah the Most High also said: 'They cannot encompass Him in knowledge.' (Ta-Ha, 110).
short_answer: Ilhad (Deviation): Shirk, Tashbih (anthropomorphism), Ta'til (negation).

question: Are all types of Tawhid (monotheism) so inextricably linked that something incompatible with one type is also incompatible with all these types as a whole?
answer: Yes, they are indeed inextricably interconnected, and therefore one who falls into polytheism in one matter becomes a polytheist in all others. An example of this is supplicating to anyone other than Allah and asking someone for something that is only within Allah's power. Such supplications are not merely worship; they are the very essence of worship that is dedicated to other than Allah and is polytheism incompatible with recognizing that divinity belongs only to Allah. As for requests for the fulfillment of needs related to seeking benefit or repelling harm when a person believes that someone other than Allah can resolve the matter, this is a manifestation of polytheism incompatible with recognizing Allah as the only Lord. This is because such a person believes that someone else alongside Allah can dispose of something in His dominion, for he turns to another with his supplications, without doubting that the other hears him from afar and near, at any time and place. Some people do not even hide such things, yet such actions are a manifestation of polytheism incompatible with the conviction that only Allah possesses specific names and attributes, for it involves recognizing that someone else can possess hearing capable of perceiving all sounds regardless of distance. Thus, manifesting polytheism in matters related to Allah's divinity inevitably leads to polytheism contradicting the recognition of Allah as the only Lord and the only possessor of specific names and attributes.
short_answer: Yes, violating one type of Tawhid destroys the others.

question: What evidence in the Quran and Sunnah indicates the obligation of belief in the angels?
answer: There is much such evidence in the Quran. For example, Allah the Most High said: 'And the angels exalt [Allah] with praise of their Lord and ask forgiveness for those on earth...' (Ash-Shura, 5). 'Those [angels] who are near your Lord are not prevented by arrogance from His worship, but they exalt Him, and to Him they prostrate.' (Al-A'raf, 206). Allah the Most High also said: 'Whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels and His messengers and Gabriel and Michael - then indeed, Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers.' (Al-Baqarah, 98). As for evidence from the Sunnah indicating the obligation of belief in angels, we have previously cited the hadith of Jibril and other hadiths. In Sahih Muslim, there is a hadith which reports that Allah the Most High created them from light, and there are a great many known hadiths about angels.
short_answer: Quranic verses (Al-Baqarah, 98) and the hadith about creation from light.
source: Ash-Shura, 5; Al-A'raf, 206; Al-Baqarah, 98; Hadith of Muslim

question: What does belief in the angels mean?
answer: It is the deep conviction that they exist and are among the creations of Allah, subject and subservient to Him, about whom Allah the Most High said: 'And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Exalted is He! Rather, they are [but] honored servants. They cannot precede Him in word, and they act by His command.' (Al-Anbiya, 26-27). '...they do not disobey Allah in what He commands them but do what they are commanded.' (At-Tahrim, 6). Allah the Most High also said: 'And those who are near Him are not prevented by arrogance from His worship, nor do they become weary. They exalt [Him] night and day [and] do not slacken.' (Al-Anbiya, 19-20). And the angels do not experience boredom or fatigue.
short_answer: Belief in their existence, obedience, and nature.

question: What categories of angels exist, from the perspective of the purpose of their creation by Allah and what He entrusted them with?
answer: Considering all the above, there are many kinds of angels: Among them is the one entrusted with delivering revelation to the messengers, and that is the Trustworthy Spirit Jibril, peace be upon him. Among them is the one entrusted with overseeing rainfall, and that is Mika'il, peace be upon him. Among them is the one entrusted with blowing the Trumpet on the Day of Resurrection, and that is Israfil, peace be upon him. Among them is the one entrusted with taking the souls of people, and that is the Angel of Death, who has assistants. Among them are those entrusted with recording the deeds of people, and these are the noble scribes. Among them are those entrusted with protecting a servant from dangers that may threaten him from front and back, and these are the accompanying angels. Among them are those entrusted with watching over Paradise and its bliss, and these are Ridwan and the angels with him. Among them are those entrusted with guarding Hell and its punishments, and these are Malik and the keepers of Hell with him, headed by nineteen angels. Among them are those entrusted with testing the deceased in the grave, and these are Munkar and Nakir. Among them are those who carry the Throne of Allah. Among them is the one entrusted with overseeing the semen in the wombs of women, observing the formation of the embryo, and recording its destiny. Among them are angels who enter the Heavenly House (Al-Bayt al-Ma'mur). Seventy thousand angels enter it every day who never return to this House again. And there are angels who travel the world, visiting gatherings where people remember Allah. And among them are those who stand in rows and do not tire. And among them are those bowing and prostrating and never rising. And besides those we have mentioned, there are others, for Allah the Most High said: 'And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him. And it is not but a reminder to humanity.' (Al-Muddaththir, 31). Quranic verses and hadiths that speak about the kinds of angels are well-known.
short_answer: Different functions: Revelation, Death, Recording deeds, Paradise/Hell, etc.

question: What indicates the obligation of belief in the Scriptures?
answer: There are many such indications. For example, Allah the Most High said: 'O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book that He sent down upon His Messenger and the Scripture which He sent down before...' (An-Nisa, 136). 'Say, "We have believed in Allah and in what was revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Descendants, and in what was given to Moses and Jesus and to the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them..."' (Al-Baqarah, 136). Many other similar verses are known. In general, it suffices to know that Allah the Most High said: 'And say, "I have believed in what Allah has revealed of the Book..."' (Ash-Shura, 15).
short_answer: Commands to believe in the revealed Books (surah An-Nisa, Al-Baqarah).

question: Are all the revealed Scriptures mentioned in the Quran?
answer: In the Quran, Allah named the following Scriptures: the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, the Scrolls of Abraham, and the Scrolls of Moses, mentioning the rest of the revealed Scriptures in general. Allah the Most High said: 'Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence. He has sent down upon you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth, confirming what was before it. And He revealed the Torah and the Gospel...' (Ali 'Imran, 2-3). '...And to David We gave the book [of Psalms].' (An-Nisa, 163). 'Or has he not been informed of what was in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham, who fulfilled [his obligations]?' (An-Najm, 36-37). 'We have already sent Our messengers with clear evidences and sent down with them the Scripture and the balance that the people may maintain [their affairs] in justice.' (Al-Hadid, 25). Thus, we must believe in all the details of what Allah said about the Scriptures in detail. As for what He mentioned in general, we must believe in it in general. And regarding what Allah and His Messenger commanded, we say: 'And say, "I have believed in what Allah has revealed of the Book..."' (Ash-Shura, 15).
short_answer: Named: Torah, Gospel, Psalms, Scrolls. In the rest, we believe in general.

question: What does belief in the Scriptures of Allah the Almighty and Majestic entail?
answer: Such belief entails a deep conviction that they are all revealed from Allah the Almighty and Majestic, and that Allah indeed spoke the words which these Scriptures contain. Among them are those whose words were heard from the Most High from behind a barrier, and they were not sent down through a messenger-angel; and among them are those which a messenger-angel conveyed to a messenger from among humans; and among them are those which Allah the Most High wrote with His own hand. Allah the Most High said: 'It is not for any human being that Allah should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a partition or that He sends a messenger to reveal, by His permission, what He wills.' (Ash-Shura, 51). And the Most High said to Musa: 'O Moses, indeed I have chosen you over the people with My messages and My words [to you].' (Al-A'raf, 144). Allah the Most High also said: '...and Allah spoke to Moses with [direct] speech.' (An-Nisa, 164). As for the Torah, Allah the Most High said about it: 'And We wrote for him on the tablets [something] of all things - instruction and explanation for all things.' (Al-A'raf, 145). And He said about 'Isa: 'And We gave him the Gospel...' (Al-Ma'idah, 46). And the Most High also said: '...and to David We gave the book [of Psalms].' (An-Nisa, 163). This was previously mentioned when discussing revelation. As for the Quran, Allah the Most High said about it: 'But Allah bears witness to that which He has revealed to you. He has sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness [as well]. And sufficient is Allah as Witness.' (An-Nisa, 166). And Allah the Most High said about it: 'And [it is] a Quran which We have separated [by intervals] that you might recite it to the people over a prolonged period. And We have sent it down progressively.' (Al-Isra, 106). And Allah the Most High also said: 'And indeed, it is the revelation of the Lord of the worlds. The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart, [O Muhammad] - that you may be of the warners - in a clear Arabic language.' (Ash-Shu'ara, 192-195). And Allah the Most High also said: 'Indeed, those who disbelieve in the message after it has come to them... And indeed, it is a mighty Book. Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it; [it is] a revelation from a [Lord who is] Wise and Praiseworthy.' (Fussilat, 41-42). There are many other similar verses.
short_answer: Conviction that they are the Words of Allah (Kalam), truly revealed.
source: Ash-Shura, 51; Al-A'raf, 144, 145; An-Nisa, 163, 164, 166; Al-Ma'idah, 46; Al-Isra, 106; Ash-Shu'ara, 192-195; Fussilat, 41-42

question: What is the status of the Quran in relation to the previously revealed Scriptures?
answer: Allah the Most High said about this: 'And We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth, confirming that which preceded it of the Scripture and as a criterion over it...' (Al-Ma'idah, 48). 'And it was not [possible] for this Quran to be produced by other than Allah, but [it is] a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of the Scripture about which there is no doubt, from the Lord of the worlds.' (Yunus, 37). Allah the Most High also said: '...and it is not a thing invented, but a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of all things and guidance and mercy for a people who believe.' (Yusuf, 111). Commentators of the Quran have indicated that the statement that the Quran contains what was revealed in previous Scriptures, testifies to it, and confirms it, means that it confirms what is true, rejects the distortions that have been introduced into these Scriptures and what has been partially or completely altered, and issues rulings abrogating the false and affirming the true. This is why all those who believed in the previous Scriptures and did not abandon their faith submit to it, as the All-Good and Most High said: 'Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it - they are believers in it. And when it is recited to them, they say, "We have believed in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were, [even] before it, Muslims [submitting to Allah]."' (Al-Qasas, 52-53). Other verses confirm this.
short_answer: Confirms the truth and abrogates previous laws (Muhaymin).

question: What must all members of the Islamic community steadfastly adhere to regarding the Quran?
answer: It is obligatory to follow it openly and secretly, hold fast to it, and give it its due right. Allah the Most High said: 'And this [Quran] is a Book We have revealed [which is] blessed, so follow it and fear Allah that you may receive mercy.' (Al-An'am, 155). 'Follow, [O mankind], what has been revealed to you from your Lord and do not follow other than Him any allies...' (Al-A'raf, 3). Allah the Most High also said: 'As for those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer - indeed, We will not allow to be lost the reward of the reformers.' (Al-A'raf, 170). This applies to the entire Quran as a whole, as indicated by many verses. As for the Prophet, ﷺ, it is reported that when advising people about the Quran, he said: '...hold fast to the Book of Allah and cling to it firmly.' (Muslim).
short_answer: Follow it, implement its rulings, and hold fast to it.

question: What does it mean to adhere to the Quran and give it its due right?
answer: It means to memorize and recite it, to engage with it day and night, to reflect upon its verses, to consider lawful what it permits and unlawful what it prohibits, to obey its commands and stay away from what it forbids, to take into account its parables and learn lessons from its stories, to act according to what is entirely clear in it, to accept what remains unclear, not to transgress the limits set in it, to defend it from the distortions of fanatics and the unfounded claims of liars, to be sincere regarding all that it speaks of, and to call to it based on knowledge.
short_answer: Recitation, reflection, acting upon it, and defending it.

question: Is the attribute of Speech an essential attribute or an attribute of action?
answer: Considering the connection of speech with the Essence of Allah the Almighty and Majestic and the circumstance that the Most High is characterized by it, this attribute is an essential attribute just like the knowledge of the Most High. However, it is also derived from His knowledge and is sent down with knowledge, for Allah knows best what He sends down. Considering the circumstance that these words are spoken by the will and desire of Allah, this attribute is an attribute of action. That is why our righteous predecessors, may Allah have mercy on them, said that the attribute of speech is both an essential attribute and an attribute of action. Allah the Most High, glory be to Him, was characterized by this attribute in pre-eternity and without beginning, as He continues to be characterized now. As for His uttering words and addressing someone, that depends on His desire and will. This means that He speaks His words if He wills, when He wills, and as He wills, giving the opportunity to hear them to whom He wills, and the speech of Allah is His attribute, not confined by any frames or limits. Allah the Most High said: 'Say, "If the sea were ink for [writing] the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as a supplement."' (Al-Kahf, 109). 'And if whatever trees upon the earth were pens and the sea [was ink], replenished thereafter by seven [more] seas, the words of Allah would not be exhausted. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.' (Luqman, 27). Allah the Most High also said: 'And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and in justice. None can alter His words, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing.' (Al-An'am, 115).
short_answer: Both essential (eternal) and of action (speaks by will).

question: What indicates the obligation of belief in the messengers?
answer: There are many such indications in the Quran and Sunnah. For example, Allah the Most High said: 'Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers and wish to discriminate between Allah and His messengers and say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and wish to adopt a way in between - those are the disbelievers, truly. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment. But those who believe in Allah and His messengers and do not discriminate between any of them - to those He is going to give their rewards...' (An-Nisa, 150-152). As for the Prophet, ﷺ, it is reported that he said: 'I have believed in Allah and His Messengers.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim).
short_answer: Verses about the disbelief of those who reject messengers (An-Nisa, 150-152).

question: What does belief in the messengers entail?
answer: Such belief entails a deep conviction that Allah the Most High sent messengers to every nation from among the people of that nation, and these messengers called them to worship Allah alone and to disbelieve in what they worshipped besides Him; that all these messengers were truthful and trustworthy, well-mannered and rightly guided, pious and noble, God-fearing and faithful; that they pointed to the straight path and were guided by it; that their Lord aided them with clear proofs and evident signs; and that they conveyed to people everything with which Allah sent them, without concealing, altering, adding a single letter from themselves, or omitting anything. Allah the Most High said: 'And [We sent] messengers about whom We have related [their stories] to you before and messengers about whom We have not related to you.' (An-Nisa, 164). And such belief entails conviction that all of them adhered to manifest truth, and that Allah the Most High chose Ibrahim as His intimate friend (Khalil), just as He chose Muhammad, ﷺ, and that He spoke to Musa directly, and that He raised Idris to a high station, and that 'Isa was the servant of Allah, His messenger, and a word from Him which He bestowed upon Maryam, and a spirit from Him; and that Allah preferred some of them over others, raising some of them by many degrees.
short_answer: Belief in their mission, truthfulness, and complete conveyance of the message.

question: Were the calls of the messengers consistent in what they commanded and prohibited people?
answer: The calls of all messengers, from the first to the last, were no different from each other if we speak about the foundations of worship, i.e., Tawhid (monotheism), which requires dedicating all types of worship, whether related to beliefs, words, or deeds, to Allah the Most High alone, and disbelieving in everything worshipped besides Allah. As for obligations such as prayer, fasting, etc., which are means of worship, some people may have been obligated with what others were not, just as some things may have been prohibited for some and permitted for others. However, all this was nothing but a test from Allah the Most High, who said: '[He] who created death and life to test you [as to] which of you is best in deed...' (Al-Mulk, 2).
short_answer: In fundamentals (Tawhid) — unified; in laws (Shari'ah) — they differed.

question: What evidence indicates that there was no difference between the messengers regarding the aforementioned foundations of worship?
answer: Such evidence in the Quran is divided into two types: general and specific. As for general evidence, examples are the words of Allah the Most High: 'And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid Taghut."' (An-Nahl, 36). 'And We sent not before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that, "There is no deity except Me, so worship Me."' (Al-Anbiya, 25). 'And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers; have We made besides the Most Merciful deities to be worshipped?' (Az-Zukhruf, 45). As for specific evidence, examples are the words of Allah the Most High: 'And We had certainly sent Noah to his people, and he said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him..."' (Al-Mu'minun, 23). 'And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him..."' (Hud, 61). 'And to 'Aad [We sent] their brother Hud. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him..."' (Hud, 50). 'And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him..."' (Hud, 84). 'And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham said to his father and his people, "Indeed, I am disassociated from that which you worship, except for He who created me..."' (Az-Zukhruf, 26-27). And Allah the Most High informed that Musa said: 'Your god is only Allah, besides whom there is no deity. He has encompassed all things in knowledge.' (Ta-Ha, 98). And Allah the Most High informed that 'Isa said: '[I said], "O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord." Indeed, he who associates others with Allah – Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire...' (Al-Ma'idah, 72). And Allah the Most High said: 'Say, "I am only a warner, and there is no deity except Allah, the One, the Prevailing."' (Sad, 65). Other verses can also serve as evidence.
short_answer: All prophets called to one thing: 'Worship Allah.'
source: An-Nahl, 36; Al-Anbiya, 25; Hud, 50-84; Al-Mu'minun, 23; Az-Zukhruf, 26-27, 45; Ta-Ha, 98; Al-Ma'idah, 72; Sad, 65

question: What evidence indicates that in specific matters related to the permissible and prohibited, the religious laws to which the messengers called people differed from one another?
answer: Evidence for this is the words of Allah the Almighty and Majestic: 'For each [religious following] We have appointed a divine law and a method.' (Al-Ma'idah, 48). Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: 'The words "a divine law and a method" mean: a way and a practice.' Similar statements were made by Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi, and Abu Ishaq As-Sabi'i. In one hadith, it is reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'The prophets are like brothers from different mothers (but the same father), and their religion is one.' (Al-Bukhari). By this religion, he meant Tawhid, the religion with which Allah sent every messenger and which was mentioned in every Scripture He revealed. As for the religious laws, they differed regarding commands and prohibitions, the permissible and the prohibited, and this was done '...to test you [as to] which of you is best in deed...' (Al-Mulk, 2).
short_answer: Verse from Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:48) and the hadith about brothers in faith.

question: Has Allah told us about all the messengers in the Quran?
answer: Allah told us what was sufficient and contains guidance and admonition, after which the Most High said: 'And [We sent] messengers about whom We have related [their stories] to you before and messengers about whom We have not related to you.' (An-Nisa, 164). Therefore, we believe in all the details of what He narrated about them in detail, and we also believe in general in what He mentioned generally.
short_answer: No, not about all. We believe in all (named and unnamed).

question: Which messengers has Allah the Most High named in the Quran?
answer: The Quran named messengers such as Adam, Nuh (Noah), Idris, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim (Abraham), Isma'il (Ishmael), Ishaq (Isaac), Ya'qub (Jacob), Yusuf (Joseph), Lut (Lot), Shu'ayb, Yunus (Jonah), Musa (Moses), Harun (Aaron), Ilyas (Elijah), Zakariyya (Zachariah), Yahya (John), Al-Yasa' (Elisha), Dhul-Kifl, Dawud (David), Sulayman (Solomon), Ayyub (Job), the Tribes, 'Isa (Jesus), and Muhammad, may Allah bless and grant peace to them all.
short_answer: Enumeration of prophets mentioned in the Quran.

question: Which messengers are called 'those of firm resolve' (Ulul-'Azm)?
answer: There were five such messengers, and Allah the Almighty and Majestic mentions them individually in two places in His Book: FIRST: In Surah Al-Ahzab, where Allah the Most High says: 'And [mention, O Muhammad], when We took from the prophets their covenant and from you and from Noah and Abraham and Moses and Jesus, the son of Mary...' (Al-Ahzab, 7). SECOND: In Surah Ash-Shura, where Allah the Most High says: 'He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah and that which We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and what We enjoined upon Abraham and Moses and Jesus – to establish the religion and not be divided therein.' (Ash-Shura, 13).
short_answer: Five: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, 'Isa, Muhammad.

question: Who was the first messenger?
answer: The first of them after differences arose among people was Nuh, as Allah the Most High said about this: 'Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him...' (An-Nisa, 163). Allah the Most High also said: 'The people of Noah denied before them, and the [disbelieving] factions after them...' (Ghafir, 5).
short_answer: Nuh (peace be upon him).

question: When did the aforementioned differences arise?
answer: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: 'Ten centuries separated Nuh from Adam, during which they adhered to the law sent down from Allah. Then differences arose among them, and Allah the Most High said: "[Mankind was] one community; then Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good tidings and warners..."' (Al-Baqarah, 213).
short_answer: Ten centuries after Adam.

question: Who is the last prophet and what indicates this?
answer: The last prophet is Muhammad, ﷺ. Allah the Most High said: 'Muhammad is not the father of [any] one of your men, but [he is] the Messenger of Allah and seal of the prophets.' (Al-Ahzab, 40). As for the Prophet, ﷺ, it is reported that he said: 'There will appear among my Ummah thirty liars, each of whom will claim to be a prophet, but I am the last of the prophets, and there will be no prophet after me.' (At-Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud, Ahmad - part of a long hadith). It is also reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, once asked 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: 'Do you not want to have the same position with me as Harun had with Musa, except that there will be no prophet after me?' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). In the hadith about the Dajjal, the Prophet, ﷺ, said: '...and I am the last of the prophets, and there will be no prophet after me.' (At-Tirmidhi). Many other similar examples are known.
short_answer: Muhammad ﷺ. Evidence: Surah Al-Ahzab, 40 and hadiths.
source: Al-Ahzab, 40; At-Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud, Ahmad, Al-Bukhari, Muslim

question: How did our Prophet Muhammad, ﷺ, differ from other prophets?
answer: He, ﷺ, differed from others in many ways, which can be classified as follows: As we mentioned, he was the last prophet. Moreover, he, ﷺ, is the master of the children of Adam, as indicated by one interpretation of the words of the Most High: 'Those messengers – some of them We caused to exceed others. Among them were those to whom Allah spoke, and He raised some of them in degree...' (Al-Baqarah, 253). Evidence for this is the Prophet's words: 'I am the master of the children of Adam, (but) I am not proud.' (At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Ahmad, Abu Dawud). Furthermore, he, ﷺ, was sent to all mankind and jinn, as indicated by the words of the Most High: 'Say, "O mankind, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you all..."' (Al-A'raf, 158). And Allah the Most High also said: 'And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind as a bringer of good tidings and a warner.' (Saba, 28). It is reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'I have been given five (things) which were not given to anyone before me: I have been aided by terror (which is cast into the hearts of my enemies) for a distance of one month's journey; the earth has been made for me a place of prayer and a means of purification, so wherever a man of my Ummah is when the time of prayer comes, let him pray; booty has been made lawful for me, which was not lawful for anyone before me; I have been given the right of intercession; and (previously) every prophet was sent only to his own people, but I have been sent to all mankind.' (Al-Bukhari). The Prophet, ﷺ, also possessed many other distinctive features that we have not mentioned and which are mentioned in many hadiths.
short_answer: Last prophet, master of the children of Adam, sent to all, granted intercession, etc.

question: What are the miracles of the prophets?
answer: Miracles are supernatural phenomena related to proof that have no parallel in ordinary life. Among them were those that could be perceived by the senses, i.e., seen or heard, such as the emergence of a she-camel from a rock, the staff turning into a serpent, inanimate objects speaking, and so on. And among them are spiritual miracles, perceived through knowledge, such as the miracle of the Quran. As for our Prophet, ﷺ, he was given the ability to perform miracles of all kinds, and whatever miracles any previous prophet performed, he was invariably granted the ability to perform something greater of its kind. Among the miracles perceptible to people are the splitting of the moon, the palm trunk weeping, water gushing forth from between his fingers, a cooked sheep leg speaking, food glorifying Allah, and many authentic reports of his other miracles. However, they are similar to the miracles performed by other prophets, which ceased when their time ended, leaving nothing but memories. As for the eternal and enduring miracle, it is the Quran, a miracle that does not cease and about which it is said: 'Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it; [it is] a revelation from a [Lord who is] Wise and Praiseworthy.' (Fussilat, 42).
short_answer: Supernatural signs. The greatest miracle is the Quran.

question: What indicates the inimitability of the Quran?
answer: It is well known that the Blessed Quran was revealed in parts over more than twenty years. Evidence of its inimitability is that throughout this time it challenged the most eloquent people, addressing them with such words: 'Then let them produce a statement like it, if they should be truthful.' (At-Tur, 34). And in the Quran it also says: 'Or do they say, "He invented it"? Say, "Then bring ten surahs like it that have been invented and call upon [for assistance] whomever you can besides Allah, if you should be truthful."' (Hud, 13). And in the Quran it also says: 'Or do they say, "He invented it"? Say, "Then bring a surah like it and call upon [for assistance] whomever you can besides Allah, if you should be truthful."' (Yunus, 38). Yet none of them did so, despite their strong desire to respond by any means possible, and despite the fact that the letters and words of the Quran were similar to the letters and words they used in their communication, competing with each other in eloquence and boasting about it. Then in the Quran, words were revealed addressing these people, showing their weakness and the inimitability of the Book of Allah, who said: 'Say, "If mankind and the jinn gathered to produce the like of this Quran, they could not produce the like of it, even if they were to each other assistants."' (Al-Isra, 88). As for the Prophet, ﷺ, he said: 'There was no prophet among the prophets but was given miracles because of which people believed. But what I have been given is only the revelation which Allah has revealed to me. So I hope that my followers will be more than those of any other prophet on the Day of Resurrection.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). People have written many books about the inimitability of the Quran from the perspective of its rhetorical style, its meanings, and its reports of past and future events, but all they have written is only a tiny part of what could be said about the Quran.
short_answer: The inability of humans and jinn to produce something like the Quran (Tahaddi).
source: At-Tur, 34; Hud, 13; Yunus, 38; Al-Isra, 88; Hadith (Al-Bukhari, Muslim)

question: What indicates the obligation of belief in the Last Day?
answer: Allah the Most High said: 'Indeed, those who do not expect the meeting with Us and are satisfied with the life of this world and feel secure therein and those who are heedless of Our signs – for those their refuge will be the Fire because of what they used to earn.' (Yunus, 7-8). 'Indeed, the promise of your Lord will be fulfilled.' (Adh-Dhariyat, 5-6). Allah the Most High also said: 'Indeed, the Hour is coming – no doubt about it...' (Ghafir, 59). Other verses could be cited as evidence.
short_answer: Numerous Quranic verses about the inevitability of Judgment.

question: What does belief in the Last Day entail and what does it include?
answer: Such belief entails a deep conviction that this Day will inevitably come, and performing actions consistent with such conviction. As for its components, they include belief in the signs that will precede the Hour, which will certainly occur before it; belief in death and in the trials, punishments, and bliss of the grave that follow it; belief in the Trumpet Blast and the emergence of people from the graves; belief in the horrors of the Day of Resurrection; belief in everything mentioned about the gathering, the records of deeds, the Scales, the Bridge (Siraat), the Pond, intercession, and all other matters; and belief in Paradise with its bliss, the highest of which will be seeing the Countenance of Allah the Almighty and Majestic, and in Hell with its punishments, the worst of which will be the separation of those who are there from their Almighty and Majestic Lord.
short_answer: Belief in the signs of the Hour, death, the grave, resurrection, judgment, Paradise, and Hell.

question: Does anyone know when the Hour will occur?
answer: Knowledge of the occurrence of the Hour is among what is called 'the keys of the unseen,' known only to Allah the Most High, as the Most High Himself said: 'Indeed, Allah [alone] has knowledge of the Hour and sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs. And no soul perceives what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul perceives in what land it will die. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Aware.' (Luqman, 34). 'They ask you, [O Muhammad], about the Hour: when is its arrival? Say, "Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None will reveal its time except Him. It lays heavily upon the heavens and the earth. It will not come upon you except unexpectedly."' (Al-A'raf, 187). Allah the Most High also said: 'They ask you about the Hour: when is its arrival? But what [concern] have you with its mention? To your Lord is its finality.' (An-Nazi'at, 42-44). And when Jibril asked the Prophet, ﷺ, 'Inform me about the Hour,' he replied: 'The one questioned about it knows no more than the questioner,' then he enumerated the signs of its approach. In another version of this hadith, it is reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: '(Knowledge of the Hour) is among the five things that no one knows except Allah the Most High,' then he recited the aforementioned verse. (Al-Bukhari, Muslim - part of a long hadith).
short_answer: No, this knowledge belongs to Allah alone.
source: Luqman, 34; Al-A'raf, 187; An-Nazi'at, 42-44; Hadith of Jibril

question: What examples of signs of the Hour's approach are mentioned in the Quran?
answer: Examples are the words of Allah the Most High: 'Do they await except that the angels should come to them or your Lord should come or that there should come some of the signs of your Lord? The Day that some of the signs of your Lord will come no soul will benefit from its faith unless it had believed before or had earned through its faith some good.' (Al-An'am, 158). 'And when the word befalls them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth speaking to them, [saying] that the people were, of Our verses, not certain [in faith].' (An-Naml, 82). '... until when Gog and Magog have been opened and they, from every elevation, descend. And [when] the true promise has approached...' (Al-Anbiya, 96-97). 'Then watch for the Day when the sky will bring a visible smoke...' (Ad-Dukhan, 10). Allah the Most High also said: 'O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the [final] Hour is a terrible thing.' (Al-Hajj, 1).
short_answer: The Beast from the earth, Gog and Magog, the Smoke.

question: What examples of signs of the Hour's approach are mentioned in the Sunnah?
answer: Examples include hadiths about the sun rising from the west, hadiths about the Beast, hadiths about various tribulations like the appearance of the Dajjal (Antichrist) and bloody battles, and hadiths about the coming of 'Isa. Also, examples include hadiths about the emergence of Gog and Magog, hadiths about the Smoke, hadiths containing reports about a wind that will take every believer, hadiths about the appearance of a fire, hadiths about the earth collapsing, and many others.
short_answer: Sun rising from the west, Dajjal, 'Isa, Gog and Magog, Smoke, Fire, etc.

question: What indicates the obligation of belief in death?
answer: Allah the Most High said: 'Say, "The angel of death, who has been entrusted with you, will take you. Then to your Lord you will be returned."' (As-Sajdah, 11). 'Every soul will taste death, and you will only be given your [full] compensation on the Day of Resurrection.' (Ali 'Imran, 185). And Allah the Most High said to His Prophet, ﷺ: 'Indeed, you are to die, and indeed, they are to die.' (Az-Zumar, 30). 'And We granted not to any man before you eternity [on earth]; so if you die – would they be eternal?' (Al-Anbiya, 34). 'Everyone upon the earth will perish, and there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor.' (Ar-Rahman, 26-27). 'Everything will be destroyed except His Face.' (Al-Qasas, 88). Allah the Most High also said: 'And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die...' (Al-Furqan, 58). Other verses could be cited as examples. This is also mentioned in numerous hadiths, and it is an obvious and well-known matter that no one doubts. However, things like stubbornness and arrogance exist, so only the actions of the sincere servants of Allah conform to belief in death and what follows it. We believe that everyone who dies, whether killed or departing this world for any other reason, leaves life precisely at their appointed term. Allah the Most High also said: '...And when their term has come, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede [it].' (Al-A'raf, 34).
short_answer: Verses about the inevitability of death and the appointed term.
source: As-Sajdah, 11; Ali 'Imran, 185; Az-Zumar, 30; Al-Anbiya, 34; Ar-Rahman, 26-27; Al-Qasas, 88; Al-Furqan, 58; Al-A'raf, 34

question: What indications about the trials of the grave and the bliss or punishment awaiting people there are mentioned in the Qur’an?
answer: The Almighty Allah said: “When death comes to one of them, he says: ‘My Lord! Send me back so that I may do righteousness in what I left behind!’ No! It is only a word he speaks, and behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected.” (Al-Mu’minun, 99–100). “... and the people of Pharaoh were afflicted with the worst torment — the Fire, to which they are exposed morning and evening. And on the Day when the Hour will be established: ‘Make the people of Pharaoh enter the severest punishment!’” (Ghafir, 45–46). “Allah will make firm those who believe with the firm word in the worldly life and in the Hereafter...” (Ibrahim, 27). “If you could but see the wrongdoers in the throes of death, while the angels stretch forth their hands, saying: ‘Release your souls! Today you will be recompensed with the humiliating punishment...’” (Al-An‘am, 93). The Almighty Allah also said: “... We know them, and We will punish them twice; then they will be returned to a great punishment.” (At-Tawbah, 101). Other verses could also be cited as examples.
short_answer: Verses about Barzakh, Pharaoh’s torment in the grave, and the strengthening of believers.

question: What indications are there in the Sunnah regarding the trials of the grave and the bliss or torment awaiting people there?
answer: There are very many authentic hadiths indicating this. Among them is the hadith narrated by Anas (may Allah be pleased with him). Anas reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'When a servant (of Allah) is placed in his grave and his companions leave him, and he hears the beat of their sandals, two angels come to him, make him sit up, and ask him: "What did you say about this man, Muhammad (ﷺ)?" The believer will answer: "I testify that he is the slave of Allah and His Messenger." Then it will be said to him: "Look at your place in the Fire; Allah has replaced it for you with a place in Paradise," and he will see both places. As for the hypocrite and the disbeliever, when he is asked: "What did you say about this man?", he will answer: "I do not know, I used to say what the people said!" Then it will be said to him: "You did not know and you did not read!" Then he will be struck with an iron hammer, and he will let out a scream that will be heard by everything near him except the jinn and mankind.' (Muslim). Also among them is the hadith narrated by Abdullah bin Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both). He reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Verily, when one of you dies, his seat is shown to him morning and evening. If he is one of the people of Paradise, then (he is shown his seat) among the people of Paradise; if he is one of the people of the Fire, then (he is shown his seat) among the people of the Fire, and it is said to him: "This is your seat until Allah resurrects you on the Day of Resurrection!"' (Muslim). Also among them is the well-known hadith in which it is reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Verily, both of them are being punished...' Also among them is the hadith narrated by Abu Ayyub (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: 'Once the Prophet (ﷺ) went out after sunset, heard a (terrifying) sound and said: "These are the Jews being punished in their graves."' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). Also among them is the hadith narrated by Asma (may Allah be pleased with her), who reported that once the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) addressed the people with a sermon, mentioning the trial to which a person will be subjected in his grave, and when he spoke about this, the Muslims began to cry loudly. (Al-Bukhari). Also among them is the hadith narrated by Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: 'I never saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finish a prayer without seeking refuge with Allah from the torment of the grave.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). And among them is the account of the solar eclipse, where it is reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded the people to supplicate to Allah for protection from the torment of the grave.
short_answer: Interrogation by two angels (Munkar and Nakir), showing the place in Paradise/Hell, torment of sinners.

question: What indications exist that people will be resurrected and rise from their graves?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'O mankind! If you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then (remember that) verily! We have created you from dust, then from a Nutfah (mixed drops of male and female sexual discharge), then from a clot (a piece of thick coagulated blood), then from a little lump of flesh, some formed and some unformed, that We may make (it) clear to you. And We cause whom We will to remain in the wombs for an appointed term, then We bring you out as infants, then (give you growth) that you may reach your age of full strength. And among you there is he who dies (young), and among you there is he who is brought back to the miserable old age, so that he knows nothing after having known. And you see the earth barren, but when We send down water (rain) on it, it is stirred (to life), it swells and puts forth every lovely kind (of growth). That is because Allah, He is the Truth, and it is He Who gives life to the dead, and it is He Who is Able to do all things. And surely, the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it, and certainly, Allah will resurrect those who are in the graves.' (Al-Hajj, 5-7). 'And He it is Who originates the creation, then will repeat it; and this is easier for Him.' (Ar-Rum, 27). '...As We began the first creation, We shall repeat it.' (Al-Anbiya, 104). 'And man says: "When I am dead, shall I then be raised alive?" Does not man remember that We created him before, while he was nothing?' (Maryam, 66-67). 'Does not man see that We have created him from Nutfah (mixed drops of male and female sexual discharge). Yet behold! He (stands forth) as an open opponent. And he puts forth for Us a parable, and forgets his own creation. He says: "Who will give life to these bones when they have rotted away and became dust?" Say: "He will give life to them Who created them for the first time! And He is the All-Knower of every creation!" He, Who produces for you fire out of the green tree, when behold! You kindle therewith. Is not He, Who created the heavens and the earth Able to create the like of them? Yes, indeed! He is the All-Knowing Supreme Creator. Verily, His Command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be!" and it is! So Glorified is He and Exalted above all that they associate with Him, and in Whose Hands is the dominion of all things, and to Him you shall be returned.' (Ya-Sin, 77-83). 'See they not that Allah, Who created the heavens and the earth, and was not wearied by their creation, is Able to give life to the dead? Yes, He surely is Able to do all things.' (Al-Ahqaf, 33). Allah the Almighty also said: 'And among His Signs (in this), that you see the earth barren, but when We send down water to it, it is stirred to life and growth. Verily, He Who gives it life, surely, (He) is Able to give life to the dead. Indeed! He is Able to do all things.' (Fussilat, 39). Other verses could also be cited as examples. Allah the Almighty often cites the example of how He revives the earth with water, and the earth, which was previously dead and dry, swells and becomes covered with green vegetation. Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Between the two blowings of the trumpet, there will be forty.' When Abu Hurairah was asked if it meant days, months, or years, he refused to answer. And he reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Then Allah will send down water from the sky, and (people) will grow like vegetation grows. There is nothing of the human body that does not decay except one bone; that is the tailbone, and from it the creation will be assembled on the Day of Resurrection.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim).
short_answer: Verses about re-creation and the example of reviving the earth with rain.
source: Al-Hajj, 5-7; Ar-Rum, 27; Al-Anbiya, 104; Maryam, 66-67; Ya-Sin, 77-83; Al-Ahqaf, 33; Fussilat, 39; Al-Bukhari, Muslim

question: What is the ruling regarding someone who does not believe in the Resurrection?
answer: Such a person does not believe in Allah the Almighty and Majestic, nor in His Books, nor in His Messengers, for Allah the Almighty said: 'And those who disbelieve say: "When we have become dust, we and our fathers, shall we really be brought forth (from the graves)?"' (An-Naml, 67). 'And if you are astonished, then astonishing is their saying: "When we are dust, shall we indeed be (raised) in a new creation?" They are those who disbelieve in their Lord! They are those round whose necks will be iron collars, and they will be dwellers of the Fire to abide therein.' (Ar-Ra'd, 5). Allah the Almighty also said: 'The disbelievers pretend that they will never be resurrected. Say: "Yes! By my Lord, you will certainly be resurrected, then you will be informed of (and recompensed for) what you did, and that is easy for Allah."' (At-Taghabun, 7). In both "Sahihs" a hadith is cited from Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him), who reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Allah the Almighty said: "The son of Adam denied Me, and he had no right to do so, and he reviled Me, and he had no right to do so. As for his denying Me, it is his saying: 'He will not bring me back to life as He created me the first time,' (though the initial creation is no easier for Me than the resurrection). As for his reviling Me, it is his saying: 'Allah has taken a son,' while I am the One, the Eternal Refuge, I beget not nor was I begotten, and there is none comparable unto Me!"' (Al-Bukhari).
short_answer: This is disbelief (Kufr).

question: What is the indication regarding the Trumpet blast, and how many times will the Trumpet be blown on the Day of Resurrection?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'And the Trumpet will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and all who are on the earth will swoon away, except him whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown a second time and behold, they will be standing, looking on (waiting).' (Az-Zumar, 68). Thus, two blasts are mentioned in this verse: after the first, all living beings will swoon (die), and after the second, they will be resurrected. Allah the Almighty also said: 'And (remember) the Day on which the Trumpet will be blown and all who are in the heavens and all who are on the earth, will be terrified, except him whom Allah wills.' (An-Naml, 87). Those who interpreted the fear mentioned in this verse as an indication that all living things will be struck down refer to the first blast, as mentioned in the verse from Surah Az-Zumar cited above. Confirmation of this is found in a hadith in Sahih Muslim, where the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Then the Trumpet will be blown, and no one will hear it but he will tilt his neck and raise it. The first to hear it will be a man who is plastering the trough for his camels, and he will swoon, and the people will swoon. Then Allah will send (or send down) rain like dew, and the bodies of the people will grow from it. Then the Trumpet will be blown again, and behold, they will stand up, looking on.' (Muslim).
short_answer: Two Trumpet blasts: 1. Swooning (Death). 2. Resurrection.

question: How is the Gathering of people on the Day of Resurrection described in the Quran?
answer: Many verses of the Quran are dedicated to describing this gathering. For example, Allah the Almighty said: 'And truly you have come unto Us alone (without wealth, companions or anything else) as We created you the first time...' (Al-An'am, 94). '...and We shall gather them all together so as to leave not one of them behind.' (Al-Kahf, 47). 'The Day We shall gather the Muttaqun (pious) unto the Most Beneficent (Allah), like a delegate (presented with honor). And We shall drive the Mujrimun (criminals, polytheists, sinners) to Hell, in a thirsty state.' (Maryam, 85-86). 'And you (all) will be in three kinds (i.e. separate groups): The foremost (in faith/good deeds) will be the foremost. And the companions of the Right Hand, - who will be the companions of the Right Hand? And the companions of the Left Hand - who will be the companions of the Left Hand?' (Al-Waqi'ah, 7-10). 'On that Day they shall follow the Caller, no crookedness (will they show) to him; and all voices shall be humbled for the Most Beneficent (Allah), and nothing shall you hear but the low voice of their footsteps.' (Ta-Ha, 108). This means that people will submissively follow to the place of gathering, treading softly like camels. Allah the Almighty also said: 'And he whom Allah guides, he is led aright; but he whom He sends astray, for such you will find no Auliya' (helpers and protectors), besides Him, and We shall gather them together on the Day of Resurrection on their faces...' (Al-Isra, 97). There are many other verses describing the Gathering on the Day of Resurrection.
short_answer: Gathering of everyone without exception. The righteous with honor, the sinners humiliated.
source: Al-An'am, 94; Al-Kahf, 47; Maryam, 85-86; Al-Waqi'ah, 7-10; Ta-Ha, 108; Al-Isra, 97

question: How is the Gathering of people on the Day of Resurrection described in the Sunnah?
answer: It is reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: '(On the Day of Resurrection) the people will be gathered in three ways: (the first way) willing and fearing; (the second way) two on a camel, three on a camel, four on a camel, and ten on a camel; as for the rest, the Fire will gather them, staying with them where they spend the night, staying with them where they take their midday rest, staying with them where they spend the morning, and staying with them where they spend the evening.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). Anas bin Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that a man asked the Prophet (ﷺ): "How will the disbeliever be gathered on his face?" He replied: 'Is not He Who made him walk on his two legs in this world Able to make him walk on his face on the Day of Resurrection?' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is also reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'You will be gathered barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised,' after which he recited the verse: '...As We began the first creation, We shall repeat it...' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). Then he said: 'The first to be clothed on the Day of Resurrection will be Ibrahim...' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is reported that Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about this: "O Messenger of Allah, will men and women look at each other?!" He replied: 'The matter will be too serious for them to care about that.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim).
short_answer: Barefoot, naked, uncircumcised. The Fire will drive the sinners.

question: How does the Quran describe the situation of those standing in waiting for Judgment (Al-Mawqif) on the Day of Resurrection?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'Consider not that Allah is unaware of that which the Zalimun (polytheists, wrong-doers, etc.) do, but He gives them respite up to a Day when the eyes will stare in horror. (They will be) hastening forward with necks outstretched, their heads raised up (towards the sky), their gaze returning not towards them and their hearts empty (from thinking because of extreme fear).' (Ibrahim, 42-43). '...The Day that the Spirit (Jibrael) and the angels will stand forth in rows, none shall speak except him whom the Most Beneficent (Allah) allows, and he will speak what is right.' (An-Naba, 38). 'And warn them of the Day that is drawing near, when the hearts will be choking the throats, and they can neither return them (hearts) to their chests nor can they throw them out. There will be no friend, nor an intercessor for the Zalimun (polytheists, wrong-doers, etc.), who could be given heed to.' (Ghafir, 18). '...in a Day the measure whereof is fifty thousand years.' (Al-Ma'arij, 4). Allah the Almighty also said: 'We shall attend to you, O you two classes (jinns and men)!' (Ar-Rahman, 31). And other verses could be cited as examples.
short_answer: Fear, silence, duration of 50,000 years.

question: How does the Sunnah describe the situation of those standing in waiting for Judgment on the Day of Resurrection?
answer: There are many hadiths describing this. One of them is narrated by Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), who reported regarding the words of the Almighty: '...The Day when (all) mankind will stand before the Lord of the 'Alamin (mankind, jinns and all that exists)' (Al-Mutaffifin, 6) — the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Some of them will stand submerged in their own sweat up to the middle of their ears.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). Another hadith is known from Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him), in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'On the Day of Resurrection, the people will sweat so much that their sweat will sink seventy cubits into the earth and will rise to reach their mouths and ears.' Many other hadiths of this kind are also known.
short_answer: Submerged in their own sweat due to terror and crowding.

question: How are the Presentation (Al-'Ard) and the Reckoning (Al-Hisab) described in the Quran?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'That Day shall you be brought to Judgment, not a secret of you will be hidden.' (Al-Haqqah, 18). 'And they will be set before your Lord in (lines as) rows, (and Allah will say): "Now indeed, you have come to Us as We created you the first time."' (Al-Kahf, 48). '...And (remember) the Day when We shall gather out of every nation a troop of those who denied Our Ayat (proofs, evidences, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.), and they (all) shall be gathered (and driven to the place of reckoning), till, when they come (before their Lord at the place of reckoning), He will say: "Did you deny My Ayat whereas you comprehended them not by knowledge (that they were the truth), or what was it that you used to do?" And the Word (of torment) will be fulfilled against them, because they have done wrong, and they will be unable to speak (in order to excuse themselves).' (An-Naml, 83-85). 'That Day mankind will proceed in scattered groups that they may be shown their deeds. So whosoever does good equal to the weight of an atom (or a small ant), shall see it. And whosoever does evil equal to the weight of an atom (or a small ant), shall see it.' (Az-Zalzalah, 6-8). 'So, by your Lord (O Muhammad ﷺ), We shall certainly call all of them to account. For all that they used to do.' (Al-Hijr, 92-93). Allah the Almighty also said: 'And stop them; verily they are to be questioned.' (As-Saffat, 24). And other verses could be cited as examples.
short_answer: Revealing of secrets, full account for every deed.
source: Al-Haqqah, 18; Al-Kahf, 48; An-Naml, 83-85; Az-Zalzalah, 6-8; Al-Hijr, 92-93; As-Saffat, 24

question: How are the Presentation and Reckoning described in the Sunnah?
answer: This is mentioned in many hadiths. For example, it is reported that when the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever is called to account will be punished,' Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) asked: "Does not Allah the Almighty say: 'He surely will receive an easy reckoning' (Al-Inshiqaq, 8)?" (To this the Prophet ﷺ) said: 'That is (only) the Presentation!' (Al-Bukhari, At-Tirmidhi, Ahmad). It is also reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'On the Day of Resurrection, a disbeliever will be brought, and it will be said to him: "Tell Me, if you had enough gold to fill the whole earth, would you ransom yourself with it?" He will say: "Yes!" Then it will be said to him: "You were asked for something easier than that!"' In another version, it is reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: '...and then it will be said: "When you were in the loins of Adam, I asked you for something easier than that: that you should not associate anything in worship with Me, but you refused (everything) except Shirk (polytheism)!"' (Al-Bukhari, Ahmad). It is also reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'There is none among you but his Lord will speak to him without an interpreter between them. He will look to his right and see nothing but what he had sent forth (of deeds), and he will look to his left and see nothing but what he had sent forth, and he will look in front of him and see nothing but the Fire. So protect yourselves from the Fire, even with half a date, or even with a good word!' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is also reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'One of you will come close to his Lord until He covers him (with His Screen), then He will say: "You did such-and-such," and (the person) will say: "Yes." And He will say: "You did such-and-such," and (the person) will say: "Yes," and He will make him confess his sins, and then He will say: "Verily, I concealed you in the world, and I forgive you today!"' (Al-Bukhari). Other hadiths can also serve as examples.
short_answer: Dialogue with Allah without intermediaries. Full audit equals punishment.

question: How is the unfolding of the scrolls described in the Quran?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'And We have fastened every man's deeds to his neck, and on the Day of Resurrection, We shall bring out for him a book which he will find open. (It will be said to him): "Read your book. You yourself are sufficient as a reckoner against you this Day."' (Al-Isra, 13-14). 'And when the written pages of deeds (good and bad) of every person are laid open...' (At-Takwir, 10). 'And the Book (one's Record) will be placed (in the right hand for a believer in the Oneness of Allah, and in the left hand for a disbeliever), and you will see the Mujrimun (criminals, polytheists, sinners, etc.), fearful of that which is (recorded) therein. They will say: "Woe to us! What sort of Book is this that leaves neither a small thing nor a big thing, but has recorded it with numbers!" And they will find all that they did, placed before them, and your Lord treats no one with injustice.' (Al-Kahf, 49). 'Then as for him who will be given his Record in his right hand will say: "Take, read my Record! Surely, I did believe that I shall meet my Account!" So he shall be in a life, well-pleasing. In a lofty Paradise, the fruits in bunches whereof will be low and near at hand. Eat and drink at ease for that which you have sent on before you in days past! But as for him who will be given his Record in his left hand, will say: "I wish that I had not been given my Record! And that I had never known how my Account is! I wish, would that it had been my end (death)! My wealth has not availed me, my power and arguments (to defend myself) have gone from me!" (It will be said): "Seize him and fetter him, then throw him in the blazing Fire. Then fasten him with a chain whereof the length is seventy cubits!" Verily, he used not to believe in Allah, the Most Great, and urged not on the feeding of Al-Miskin (the poor)! So no friend has he here this Day, nor any food except filth from the washing of wounds, none will eat it except the Khati'un (sinners, disbelievers, polytheists, etc.).' (Al-Haqqah, 19-37). 'Then, as for him who will be given his Record in his right hand...' (Al-Inshiqaq, 7). 'But as for him who will be given his Record behind his back...' (Al-Inshiqaq, 10). These words indicate that if a person's book is given to his right hand, it will be given from the front, but for the one to whom it is given in his left hand, it will be given from behind, and we ask Allah the Almighty and Majestic for protection from that!
short_answer: Book in the right hand means Paradise; in the left (or behind) means Hell.

question: How is the unfolding of the scrolls described in the Sunnah?
answer: This is mentioned in many hadiths. For example, it is reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'The believer will be brought close to his Lord until He covers him, then He will make him confess (to his sins, saying): "Do you acknowledge this sin?" He will say: "I acknowledge it," and will say: "Lord, I acknowledge it!" twice. Then He will say: "I concealed you in this world, and I forgive you today!" Then the scroll of his good deeds will be folded up. As for the others (or: ...the disbelievers), they will be called publicly before the witnesses: "These are the ones who lied against their Lord!"' (Hud, 18. Al-Bukhari). It is reported that Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: '(Once) I asked: "O Messenger of Allah, will a person remember those he loves on the Day of Resurrection?" He replied: "O Aisha, regarding three (places), he will not remember: he will not remember his beloved when standing at the Balance (until it is determined) whether his scale is heavy or light; he will not remember him when the books are distributed (until it is determined) whether he receives his book in his right hand or his left; and he will not remember when the tongues of the Fire appear."' (Ahmad, Abu Dawood (part of a long hadith)).
short_answer: Private conversation for the believer and public shame for the disbelievers.

question: Which verses of the Quran indicate that Scales will be set up on the Day of Resurrection, and how will the weighing take place?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'And We shall set up balances of justice on the Day of Resurrection, then none will be dealt with unjustly in anything. And if there be the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it. And Sufficient are We as Reckoners.' (Al-Anbiya, 47). Allah the Almighty also said: 'And the weighing on that day (Day of Resurrection) will be the true (weighing). So as for those whose scale (of good deeds) will be heavy, they will be the successful (by entering Paradise). And as for those whose scale will be light, they are those who will lose their ownselves (by entering Hell) because they denied and rejected Our Ayat (proofs, evidences, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.).' (Al-A'raf, 8-9). As for the disbelievers, Allah the Almighty also said: '...and on the Day of Resurrection, We shall not give them any weight.' (Al-Kahf, 105). Other verses also serve as examples.
short_answer: Establishment of precise Scales (Mizan).

question: Which hadiths indicate that Scales will be set up on the Day of Resurrection, and how will the weighing take place according to the Sunnah?
answer: This is mentioned in many hadiths, an example of which is the hadith about the card (Bitaqa) containing the two testimonies of faith, which will outweigh ninety scrolls of bad deeds, even though each scroll extends as far as the eye can see. Another example is what the Prophet (ﷺ) said about Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him): 'Are you amazed at the thinness of his shins? By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, on the Scales, they will be heavier than (Mount) Uhud!' (Ahmad, Al-Hakim, Al-Haythami). Another example is the hadith in which the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Verily, on the Day of Resurrection, a huge fat man will be brought, who in the sight of Allah will weigh less than the wing of a mosquito!' (Then he added): 'Read: "...and on the Day of Resurrection, We shall not give them any weight."' (Al-Kahf, 105. Al-Bukhari, Muslim). Other examples can also be cited.
short_answer: Weighing of deeds, scrolls, and the people themselves.

question: What indications regarding the Sirat (Bridge) are found in the Quran?
answer: Allah the Almighty and Great said: 'There is not one of you but will pass over it (Hell); this is with your Lord; a Decree which must be accomplished. Then We shall save those who use to fear Allah and were dutiful to Him. And We shall leave the Zalimun (polytheists and wrongdoers, etc.) therein (humbled) to their knees (in Hell).' (Maryam, 71-72). Allah the Almighty also said: 'On the Day you shall see the believing men and the believing women their light running forward before them and by their right hands...' (Al-Hadid, 12).
short_answer: Verses about passing over Hell (Maryam, 71-72).

question: What indications regarding the Sirat are found in the Sunnah and how is it described in hadiths?
answer: This is mentioned in many hadiths, for example, in the hadith of intercession, where it is reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'A bridge will be set up and placed over Hell.' People asked: "O Messenger of Allah, what is this bridge?" He replied: 'A slippery place on which there are hooks and claws and thorny plants with curved spines, similar to those that grow in Najd and are called As-Sa'dan. The believers will pass over it like the glance of an eye, like lightning, like the wind, and like fine horses. Some will be saved (unharmed), some will be saved after being scratched, and some will be piled up into the Fire of Hell, until the last of them is dragged across.' As for Abu Sa'id (Al-Khudri), may Allah be pleased with him, he said: "It has reached me that this bridge is thinner than a hair and sharper than a sword." (Al-Bukhari, Muslim (part of a long hadith)).
short_answer: Slippery bridge over Hell, thinner than a hair.

question: What indications regarding equal retribution (Al-Qisas) on the Day of Resurrection are found in the Quran?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'Surely! Allah wrongs not even of the weight of an atom (or a small ant), but if there is any good (done), He doubles it, and gives from Him a great reward.' (An-Nisa, 40). 'This Day every person shall be recompensed for what he earned. No injustice (shall be done to anybody). Truly, Allah is Swift in reckoning. And warn them (O Muhammad ﷺ) of the Day that is drawing near, when the hearts will be choking the throats, and they can neither return them (hearts) to their chests nor can they throw them out. There will be no friend, nor an intercessor for the Zalimun (polytheists, wrong-doers, etc.), who could be given heed to. Allah knows the fraud of the eyes, and all that the breasts conceal. And Allah judges with truth...' (Ghafir, 17-20). Allah the Almighty also said: '...and they will be judged with truth, and they will not be wronged.' (Az-Zumar, 69).
short_answer: Complete justice and restitution for grievances.

question: What indications regarding equal retribution on the Day of Resurrection are found in the Sunnah and what will it involve?
answer: This is mentioned in many hadiths. For example, it is reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'The first thing for which judgment will be passed among the people is regarding bloodshed.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is also reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever has wronged his brother, should ask for his pardon today, for (in the Hereafter) there will be neither Dinar nor Dirham. (He should do this) before some of his good deeds are taken and given to his brother, and if he has no good deeds, some of his brother's bad deeds will be taken and cast upon him.' (Al-Bukhari, Ahmad, Al-Baghawi). It is also reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'The believers will be saved from the Fire and will be detained on a bridge between Paradise and Hell, where they will settle their accounts with one another regarding the grievances they had in this world, and when they are cleansed and purified, they will be permitted to enter Paradise.' (Al-Bukhari). Many hadiths of this kind are known.
short_answer: Exchange of good deeds and sins (Hadith of the Bankrupt).

question: What indications regarding the Pond (Hawd) are found in the Quran, and how is it described in the Sunnah?
answer: Allah the Almighty and Great said to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): 'Verily, We have granted you Al-Kawthar.' (Al-Kawthar, 1). There is a vast number of hadiths indicating its existence. For example, it is reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'I will be at the Pond before you.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is also reported that (once) the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Verily, I shall precede you, and verily, I shall be a witness over you, and by Allah, verily, I am looking at my Pond right now!' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is also reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'My Pond is the size of a month's journey, its water is whiter than milk, its scent is more pleasant than musk, and its vessels are like the stars of the sky, and whoever drinks from it will never feel thirst again.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is also reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'I came to a river whose banks were tents of hollow pearls, and I asked: "What is this, O Jibril?" He replied: "This is Al-Kawthar."' (Al-Bukhari, Ahmad). Many other hadiths could also be cited as examples.
short_answer: Al-Kawthar in the Quran. Description of the Hawd in the Sunnah.

question: What is the indication of the obligation to believe in Paradise and Hell?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: '...then fear the Fire (Hell) whose fuel is men and stones, prepared for the disbelievers. And give glad tidings to those who believe and do righteous good deeds, that for them will be Gardens under which rivers flow (Paradise)...' (Al-Baqarah, 24-26). There are a huge number of other verses indicating this. As for the Prophet (ﷺ), it is reported that when supplicating to Allah before the voluntary night prayers, he used to say: 'All the praises are for You, You are the Truth, and Your Promise is the truth, and the Meeting with You is truth, and Your Word is the truth, and Paradise is the truth, and the Fire is the truth, and the Prophets are the truth, and Muhammad (ﷺ) is the truth, and the Hour is the truth...' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). And it is reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever testifies that there is no god but Allah alone, Who has no partner, and that Muhammad is His slave and His Messenger, and that Isa (Jesus) is the slave of Allah, His Messenger, His Word which He bestowed on Maryam, and a Spirit from Him, and that Paradise is the truth and the Fire is the truth, Allah will admit him into Paradise regardless of what his deeds were.' In another version, it is reported that the Prophet also said: '...through whichever of the eight gates of Paradise he wishes...' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim).
short_answer: They are already created and are the Truth.

question: What does belief in Paradise and Hell imply?
answer: Such belief implies a deep conviction that they are created and exist right now, and that by the Will of Allah they will remain forever and will never cease to exist. An integral part of this is also belief in the bliss of Paradise and the torment of Hell.
short_answer: They are created, exist now, and are eternal.

question: What indicates the existence of Paradise and Hell at the present time?
answer: Allah the Almighty and Great has informed us that both already exist. For example, regarding Paradise, He said: '...prepared for the Muttaqun (pious).' (Al Imran, 133). Regarding Hell, the Almighty said: '...prepared for the disbelievers.' (Al Imran, 131). The Almighty also informed us that He settled Adam and his wife in Paradise, where they remained until they ate from the forbidden tree. Furthermore, the Almighty informed us that the Fire is shown to the disbelievers in their graves morning and evening. As for the Prophet (ﷺ), it is reported that he said: 'I was shown Paradise, and I saw that the majority of its dwellers were the poor, and I was shown the Fire, and I saw that the majority of its dwellers were women.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). Earlier, when discussing the trials and torments of the grave, we cited the words of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: '...when any one of you dies, his place is shown to him...' It is also reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Delay the prayer until it gets cooler, for verily, the intensity of heat is from the exhalation of Hell...' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is also reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: '...(Once) the Fire complained to its Lord, saying: "O my Lord, some parts of me have consumed others!" So (Allah) allowed it to take two breaths: one breath in winter and one breath in summer, which is when you feel the most severe heat and the most severe cold.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is also reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Fever is from the heat of Hell, so cool it with water.' (Muslim). It is also reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'When Allah created Paradise and Hell, He sent Jibril to Paradise and said: "Look at it..."' (An-Nasa'i, At-Tirmidhi (part of a long hadith)). It is also reported that once during a solar eclipse, Paradise and Hell were shown to the Prophet (ﷺ), just as they were shown to him during the Night Journey, and there are a great many other authentic hadiths mentioning this.
short_answer: The verses 'Prepared...' and the vision of the Prophet (ﷺ).

question: What indications exist that Paradise and Hell will exist forever and never perish?
answer: As for Paradise, Allah the Almighty said: '...they will abide therein forever. That is the supreme success.' (At-Tawbah, 100). '...and they will not be removed from it.' (Al-Hijr, 48). '...a gift without an end.' (Hud, 108). '...neither cut off nor forbidden.' (Al-Waqi'ah, 33). 'Verily, this is Our Provision which will never finish.' (Sad, 54). Allah the Almighty also said: 'Verily! The Muttaqun (pious), will be in place of Security (Paradise). Among Gardens and Springs; Dressed in fine silk and (also) in thick silk, facing each other, So (it will be), and We shall marry them to Houris (female fair ones) with wide, lovely eyes. They will call therein for every kind of fruit in peace and security; They will never taste death therein except the first death (of this world), and He will save them from the torment of the blazing Fire.' (Ad-Dukhan, 51-56). Other verses could be cited indicating this. Thus, the Almighty informed about the eternity of Paradise, the eternity of the life of its inhabitants, that this life will not cease, and that they will not leave Paradise.
