The same applies to Hell, regarding which the Almighty said: '...Except the way of Hell, to dwell therein forever...' (An-Nisa, 169). 'Verily, Allah has cursed the disbelievers, and has prepared for them a flaming Fire (Hell). Wherein they will abide forever, and they will find neither a Wali (protector) nor a Helper.' (Al-Ahzab, 64-65). '...and whosoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, then verily, for him is the Fire of Hell, he shall dwell therein forever.' (Al-Jinn, 23). '...and they will never get out of the Fire.' (Al-Baqarah, 167). '...it (the torment) will not be lightened for them, and they will be plunged into destruction with deep regrets, sorrows and in despair therein.' (Az-Zukhruf, 75). 'Neither will it have a complete killing effect on them so that they die, nor shall its torment be lightened for them.' (Fatir, 36). Allah the Almighty also said: 'Verily, whoever comes to his Lord as a Mujrim (criminal, polytheist, sinner, etc.), then surely, for him is Hell, wherein he will neither die nor live.' (Ta-Ha, 74). In these and similar verses, the Almighty informed us that the inhabitants of Hell who deserve it, for whom it was created and who were created for it, will remain in it forever. And the Almighty rejected the possibility of them leaving it, saying: '...and they will never get out of the Fire.' (Al-Baqarah, 167). And He rejected the possibility that their torment would cease, saying: 'it will not be lightened for them, and they will be plunged into destruction with deep regrets...' (Az-Zukhruf, 75), just as He rejected the possibility that they would die, saying: 'Verily, whoever comes to his Lord as a Mujrim... surely, for him is Hell, wherein he will neither die nor live.' (Ta-Ha, 74). As for the Prophet (ﷺ), it is reported that he said: 'As for the people of the Fire who deserve it, verily, they will not die in it nor will they live.' (Muslim, Ahmad, Ibn Majah). It is also reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, Death will be brought and placed between Paradise and the Fire, then it will be slaughtered, and a caller will announce: "O people of Paradise, there is no death! O people of the Fire, there is no death!" Then the people of Paradise will have joy added to their joy, and the people of the Fire will have sorrow added to their sorrow (and everyone will remain eternally where they are).' In another version, it is reported that after saying this, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited the verse: 'And warn them (O Muhammad ﷺ) of the Day of grief and regrets, when the case has been decided, while (now) they are in a state of carelessness, and they believe not.' (Maryam, 39). (Al-Bukhari, Muslim).
short_answer: Verses on the eternity of Paradise and Hell and the Hadith of slaughtering Death.
source: At-Tawbah, 100; Hud, 108; An-Nisa, 169; Al-Ahzab, 64-65; Bukhari, Muslim

question: What indications exist that in the Hereafter believers will see their Most Benevolent and Most High Lord?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'Some faces that Day shall be Nadirah (shining and radiant). Looking at their Lord...' (Al-Qiyamah, 22-23). 'For those who have done good is the best (reward, i.e. Paradise) and even more (i.e. having the honor of glancing at the Countenance of Allah)...' (Yunus, 26). As for the disbelievers, Allah the Almighty said regarding them: 'Nay! Surely, they (evil-doers) will be veiled from seeing their Lord that Day.' (Al-Mutaffifin, 15). But if the enemies of Allah are veiled from Him, then those who are close to Him will not be veiled. Jarir bin Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated: "Once, when we were with the Prophet (ﷺ) on the fourteenth night of the month, he looked at the full moon and said: 'Verily, you will see your Lord as you see this moon, and you will not be harmed in seeing Him! So if you can avoid missing a prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do so.'" (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). The words of the Prophet (ﷺ), 'as you see this...', meaning 'as you see this moon', mean that one vision is likened to another, but it does not mean that one object of observation is likened to another. The same applies to the words of the Prophet (ﷺ), 'when Allah decrees a matter in heaven, the angels beat their wings in submission to His saying, (making a sound) like a chain dragging over a rock.' (Al-Bukhari and Ibn Majah). In this case, one hearing is likened to another, but what is heard in the first and second cases is not likened to each other, because Allah is above having His Essence or His Attributes likened to anything created. As for the Prophet (ﷺ), it is impossible to even imagine that his words imply anthropomorphism, for he knew Allah the Almighty and Majestic better than all people. And in the hadith narrated by Suhayb (may Allah be pleased with him), it is reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Then the veil will be lifted, and they will not be given a gift more beloved to them than looking at their Almighty and Majestic Lord,' after which he recited the following verse: 'For those who have done good is the best and even more...' (Yunus, 26). (Muslim, At-Tirmidhi). Many authentic hadiths unequivocally indicate this. As for the one who denies this, he believes neither in the Quran nor in what Allah sent His Messengers with, and such a person belongs to those about whom Allah the Almighty said: 'Nay! Surely, they will be veiled from seeing their Lord that Day...' (Al-Mutaffifin, 15). We ask Allah the Almighty for forgiveness and deliverance from such a thing, and also that He grants us the opportunity to enjoy the sight of His Face, Ameen.
short_answer: Verse: '...Looking at their Lord' and the Hadith about seeing the Lord like the Moon.

question: What is the indication for the (obligation of) belief in Intercession (Shafa'ah), who will intercede, who will be interceded for, and when will it happen?
answer: Allah the Almighty and Majestic speaks about intercession in many verses of His Book, linking it to a number of necessary conditions. For example, the Almighty informed us that He alone will control everything related to this intercession and no one else. Allah the Almighty said: 'Say: "To Allah belongs all intercession."' (Az-Zumar, 44). If we speak about when intercession will take place, the Almighty and Great informed us that it will happen only with His permission. Allah the Almighty said: '...Who is he that can intercede with Him except with His Permission?...' (Al-Baqarah, 255). 'No intercessor (can plead with Him) except after His Permission.' (Yunus, 3). 'And there are many angels in the heavens, whose intercession will avail nothing except after Allah has given leave for whom He wills and pleases.' (An-Najm, 26). '...Intercession with Him profits not, except for him whom He permits.' (Saba, 23). As for who will be allowed to address Allah with words of intercession, the Almighty informed us not only of the possibility of this solely with His permission, but also that He will not allow anyone to do so except His chosen ones. 'None shall have the power of intercession, but such a one as has received a covenant (or promise) from the Most Beneficent (Allah).' (Maryam, 87). Regarding those for whom intercession can be made, Allah informed us that He will allow intercession only for those with whom He is pleased. '...and they cannot intercede except for him with whom He is pleased...' (Al-Anbiya, 28). 'On that day no intercession shall avail, except the one for whom the Most Beneficent (Allah) has given permission and whose word is acceptable to Him.' (Ta-Ha, 109). But He, Glory be to Him, will be pleased only with the monotheists and sincere people, and concerning all others, Allah the Almighty said: 'There will be no friend, nor an intercessor for the Zalimun (polytheists, wrong-doers, etc.), who could be given heed to.' (Ghafir, 18). And Allah the Almighty also informed that on the Day of Resurrection they will say: '...Now we have no intercessors, nor a close friend!' (Ash-Shu'ara, 100-101). Allah the Almighty also said: 'So no intercession of intercessors will be of any use to them.' (Al-Muddaththir, 48). As for the Prophet (ﷺ), he informed us that he was granted the right of intercession, just as he informed us that he will come to the Throne of Allah, prostrate before it, and praise Allah with words that Allah will teach him, and he will not intercede for anyone until it is said to him: 'Raise your head and ask - it will be granted to you, and speak - it will be heard, and intercede - intercession will be granted to you.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others). Furthermore, the Prophet (ﷺ) reported that he will not be granted the right to intercede for all sinners among the monotheists at once. He said: 'He will set a limit for me, and then I will admit them into Paradise,' after which he indicated that he would return and prostrate before Allah again, and He would set a limit for him again, and so on, as mentioned in the hadith of intercession. It is reported that Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) asked the Prophet (ﷺ): "Who will be the happiest of people thanks to your intercession?" He replied: "The one who says 'There is no god but Allah' from a pure heart." (Al-Bukhari, Ahmad).
short_answer: Only with Allah's permission and for Monotheists (whom He is pleased with).

question: How many types of intercession are there, and which one will be the greatest?
answer: 1 - The greatest intercession will be on the Day of Resurrection, when people will stand at the gathering place (Mawqif) waiting for the final judgment that Allah will pass on His slaves. The right to such intercession will be granted only to our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and this is the Praiseworthy Station (Al-Maqam Al-Mahmud) promised to him by Allah the Almighty and Great, regarding which He said: '...it may be that your Lord will raise you to a Maqam Mahmud (a station of praise and glory).' (Al-Isra, 79). This refers to when it becomes unbearable for people to remain in that place any longer, their stay is prolonged, their anxiety increases, and they are submerged in their own sweat so much that it becomes difficult to breathe, they will seek intercession, wishing for Allah to pass judgment on them. They will first go to Adam, then to Nuh, then to Ibrahim, then to Musa, then to Isa son of Maryam, and each of them will say: "Myself, myself!" (meaning I am worried about myself), until they come to our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), who will say that he is ready to intercede. (Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others). 2 - Intercession which will be expressed in supplication for the gates of Paradise to be opened. The first to open them will be our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and the first nation to enter will be his nation. 3 - Intercession for those whom Allah commands to be cast into Hell, so that they do not end up there. 4 - Intercession for those people who professed the religion of Monotheism who end up in Hell. It will be expressed in supplication for them to be taken out, after which they will be taken out of Hell burnt and resembling coal, and then they will be thrown into the River of Life, and they will grow like a seed carried by a stream. 5 - Intercession aimed at raising the rank of those who enter Paradise. In the last three cases, interceding with Allah for people will be allowed not only for our Prophet (ﷺ), but he will be the first, followed by other prophets, angels, the righteous (Awliya), and young children who died before their parents, after which Allah the Almighty, by His Mercy, will take countless people out of the Fire and admit them into Paradise. 6 - Intercession aimed at lightening the torment of some disbelievers, the right of which is granted only to our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and it concerns his uncle Abu Talib, as reported in Sahih Muslim and other sources. This hadith is also cited by Al-Bukhari. It reports that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Perhaps my intercession on the Day of Resurrection will benefit him and he will be placed in a shallow part of the Fire, which will reach (only) up to his ankles and from which his brain will boil.' It is reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'They will not cease to be thrown into Hell and it will say: "Is there any more?" until the Lord of Glory places His Foot over it, and then one part of it will collapse into the other, and it will say: "Enough, enough, by Your Glory and Your Generosity!" And there will continue to be empty space in Paradise until Allah creates (new) people for it, whom He will settle in this space.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim).
short_answer: Six types. The greatest is Maqam Mahmud (start of Judgment).

question: Can anyone enter Paradise or be saved from Hell thanks to their deeds?
answer: It is reported that once the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Do good deeds properly, sincerely and moderately and know that your deeds will not make you enter Paradise.' (The people) asked: "Even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: 'Even me, unless Allah bestows His Favor and Mercy on me.' In another version, it is reported that when the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Do good deeds properly, sincerely and moderately, and rejoice, for verily, no one's deeds will admit him into Paradise,' (the people) asked: "Even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He replied: 'Even me, unless Allah bestows His Mercy on me; and know that the most beloved deed to Allah is the most regular and constant even if it were little.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim).
short_answer: No, only by the Mercy of Allah.

question: How is the aforementioned hadith reconciled with the words of the Almighty: 'And it will be cried out to them: "This is the Paradise which you have inherited for what (bi-ma) you used to do."' (Al-A'raf, 43)?
answer: Praise be to Allah, there are no contradictions between this hadith and the words of the Almighty. The fact is that the preposition "bi" (for/by/because of), used in this verse, indicates causality, for righteous deeds will be the cause of a person ending up in Paradise, and without them it would be impossible, because an effect exists only by virtue of the existence of a cause. As for the hadith, it denies that the preposition "bi" implies a price (or exchange value), because even if a slave of Allah lived until the end of time and fasted all day and prayed all night during all that time and did not commit a single sin, even then all his deeds would not equate to one-hundredth of the smallest of the apparent and hidden favors bestowed upon him by Allah. How then can they serve as payment for entering Paradise? 'My Lord! Forgive and have mercy, for You are the Best of those who show mercy!' (Al-Mu'minun, 118).
short_answer: Deeds are the cause, not the price of Paradise.

question: What is the indication for the obligation of belief in Predestination (Al-Qadar) in general?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'And the Command of Allah is a decree determined.' (Al-Ahzab, 38). '...so that Allah might accomplish a matter already ordained...' (Al-Anfal, 42). '...But the Command of Allah must be executed.' (Al-Ahzab, 37). 'No calamity befalls, but with the Leave [i.e. decision and Qadar (Divine Preordainments)] of Allah, and whosoever believes in Allah, He guides his heart.' (At-Taghabun, 11). 'And what you suffered (of the disaster) on the day (of the battle of Uhud when) the two armies met, was by the leave of Allah...' (Al Imran, 166). Allah the Almighty also said: '...but give glad tidings to As-Sabirun (the patient ones, etc.). Who, when afflicted with calamity, say: "Truly! To Allah we belong and truly, to Him we shall return." They are those on whom are the Salawat (i.e. blessings, etc.) from their Lord, and (they are those who) receive His Mercy, and it is they who are the guided-ones.' (Al-Baqarah, 155-157). Other verses can also serve as examples. And in the hadith of Jibril, it is reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: '...and that you believe in the Divine Decree (Al-Qadar), both the good and the bad thereof.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawood, Ibn Majah and An-Nasa'i). It is also reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'And know that what has befallen you was not going to miss you, and that which has missed you was not going to befall you.' (Abu Dawood, Ibn Majah, Ahmad). It is also reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: '...and if anything (in the form of trouble) comes to you, don't say: "If I had not done that, it would not have happened," but say: "Allah has ordained it and what He willed He has done."' (Muslim). It is also reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Everything is by decree, even incapacity and intelligence.' (Muslim, Ahmad, Malik). Other hadiths can also serve as examples.
short_answer: Verses about Qadar and the Hadith of Jibril.

question: Into how many levels is belief in Predestination divided?
answer: Belief in Predestination is divided into four levels: FIRST LEVEL: Belief that Allah's Knowledge encompasses everything, and nothing, even the weight of an atom, can escape Him in the heavens or on the earth; that the Almighty knew about all His creations even before He created them, and that He knew in advance what their provision and their lifespan would be, and knew what they would say and do, and knew about their movement and rest, and knew about all their apparent and hidden manifestations, and knew who among them would enter Paradise and who would end up in Hell. SECOND LEVEL: Belief that all of this was written down, in other words, that the Almighty wrote down everything He knew in advance would exist, which includes belief in the existence of the Preserved Tablet (Al-Lawh Al-Mahfuz) and belief in the Pen (Al-Qalam). THIRD LEVEL: Belief in the all-pervading Will of Allah and His Omnipotence as inseparable things, regarding what has already been and what will definitely be, and regarding what is not so, if we speak about what has not been and does not exist. Thus, whatever Allah wills inevitably comes into being by virtue of His Power, and as for what Allah does not will, it does not come into being because there is no Will of Allah for it, but not because Allah is unable to do it, for the Almighty and Great is above that. Allah the Almighty said: 'And Allah is not such that anything in the heavens or in the earth escapes Him. Verily, He is All-Knowing, All-Omnipotent.' (Fatir, 44). FOURTH LEVEL: Belief that Allah the Almighty is the Creator of everything, that there is not a single atom in the heavens or on the earth or between them of which Allah is not the Creator, and belief that He is the Creator of the actions and inaction of everything. Glory be to Him, there is no creator and lord other than Him!
short_answer: Four: Knowledge, Writing, Will, Creation.

question: What serves as an indication of the first level, which is belief in Knowledge?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'He is Allah, beside Whom La ilaha illa Huwa (none has the right to be worshipped but He), the All-Knower of the unseen and the seen.' (Al-Hashr, 22). '...that you may know that Allah has power over all things, and that Allah surrounds (comprehends) all things in (His) Knowledge.' (At-Talaq, 12). 'Those who disbelieve say: "The Hour will not come to us." Say: "Yes, by my Lord, it will come to you." (Allah, He is) the All-Knower of the unseen, not even the weight of an atom (or a small ant) or less than that or greater, escapes from His Knowledge in the heavens or in the earth, but it is in a Clear Book (Al-Lauh Al-Mahfuz).' (Saba, 3). 'And with Him are the keys of the Ghaib (all that is hidden), none knows them but He.' (Al-An'am, 59). 'Allah knows best with whom to place His Message.' (Al-An'am, 124). 'Verily, your Lord is the Best Knower of him who has gone astray from His Path, and He is the Best Knower of those who are guided.' (Al-Qalam, 7). 'Does not Allah know best those who are in the 'Alamin (mankind and jinns)?' (Al-Ankabut, 10). 'And (remember) when your Lord said to the angels: "Verily, I am going to place (mankind) generations after generations on earth." They said: "Will You place therein those who will make mischief therein and shed blood, - while we glorify You with praises and sanctify Your Holiness?" He (Allah) said: "I know that which you do not know."' (Al-Baqarah, 30). Allah the Almighty also said: '...and it may be that you dislike a thing which is good for you and that you like a thing which is bad for you. Allah knows but you do not know.' (Al-Baqarah, 216). It is reported that a man asked the Prophet (ﷺ): "O Messenger of Allah, can the people of Paradise be distinguished from the people of the Fire?" He replied: 'Yes.' (The man) asked: "Then why do they (strive to) do (good) deeds?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Everyone will do that for which he was created (or: ...that which has been facilitated for him).' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is reported that once the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about the children of polytheists, to which he replied: 'Allah knows best what they would have done.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is also reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Verily, Allah created (some) people for Paradise, creating them for it while they were still in their fathers' loins, and He created others for the Fire, creating them for it while they were still in their fathers' loins.' (Muslim, Abu Dawood, Ahmad). It is also reported that concerning this, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Verily, a man may perform deeds that seem to the people to be the deeds of the people of Paradise, while (in reality) he is among the people of the Fire, and verily, a man may perform deeds that seem to the people to be the deeds of the people of the Fire, while (in reality) he is among the people of Paradise.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is also reported regarding this that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) once said: "There is none among you whose place in Paradise or the Fire is not known." (The people) asked: "O Messenger of Allah, then why should we (strive to) do (good deeds)? Should we not rely on this?" He said: 'No, act, for everyone is facilitated towards that for which he was created,' after which he recited the following verses: 'As for him who gives (in charity) and keeps his duty to Allah and fears Him, and believes in Al-Husna, We will make smooth for him the path of ease (goodness). But he who is greedy miser and thinks himself self-sufficient, and belies Al-Husna, We will make smooth for him the path for evil.' (Al-Lail, 5-10. Al-Bukhari, Muslim). Other hadiths also serve as an indication of this.
short_answer: Verses about Allah's All-Encompassing Knowledge and hadiths about the predestination of one's place in Paradise or Hell.
source: Al-Hashr, 22; At-Talaq, 12; Saba, 3; Al-An'am, 59, 124; Al-Qalam, 7; Al-Ankabut, 10; Al-Baqarah, 30, 216; Al-Lail, 5-10; Hadiths (Bukhari, Muslim)

question: What serves as an indication of the second level, which is belief that what is predestined was written by Allah?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: '...and all things We have recorded with numbers (as a record) in a Clear Book.' (Ya-Sin, 12). 'Verily, that is (all) in the Book...' (Al-Hajj, 70). And concerning the dispute of Musa with Pharaoh, the Almighty said the following: '(Pharaoh) said: "What about the generations of old?" (Musa) said: "The knowledge thereof is with my Lord, in a Record. My Lord is neither unaware nor He forgets."' (Ta-Ha, 51-52). Allah the Almighty also said: '...And no female conceives or gives birth, but with His Knowledge. And no aged man is granted a length of life, nor is a part cut off from his life (or another man's life), but is in a Book (Al-Lauh Al-Mahfuz). Surely, that is easy for Allah.' (Fatir, 11). Other verses also serve as indications of this. As for the Prophet (ﷺ), it is reported that he said: 'There is no person whose place in Paradise or Hell has not already been written by Allah, and it is also written whether he is happy or miserable.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). In this regard, it is also reported that once Suraqa bin Malik Ibn Ju'shum (may Allah be pleased with him) asked the Prophet (ﷺ): "O Messenger of Allah, explain our religion to us as if we were created just now. Regarding what do we (perform) deeds today: regarding that which is already written and predestined, or that which (is yet to be written)?" He said: 'No, regarding that which is already written and predestined.' (Suraqa) asked: "Then why do anything at all?" Then (the Prophet ﷺ) said: 'Act, for everyone will be facilitated.' In another version of this hadith, it is reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: '...everyone will have his deeds facilitated.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). Other hadiths also serve as indications of this.
short_answer: Verses about the Preserved Tablet (the Book) and hadiths about the writing of destinies.
source: Ya-Sin, 12; Al-Hajj, 70; Ta-Ha, 51-52; Fatir, 11; Hadiths (Bukhari, Muslim)

question: How many types of predestination are included in this level?
answer: This level includes five types of predestination, and all of them are related to knowledge. FIRST (Al-Taqdir Al-Azali): Eternal predestination, in other words, the writing of everything that will happen fifty thousand years before the creation of the heavens and the earth, when Allah created the Pen (Al-Qalam). SECOND (Al-Taqdir Al-'Umri): Predestination related to the life of each individual and related to the covenant. Allah the Almighty said: 'Am I not your Lord?' (Al-A'raf, 172). THIRD: Predestination which is also related to life in general, but refers to the moment when the seed is placed in the woman's womb. FOURTH: Predestination, the effect of which extends to the coming year and is revealed to the angels on the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr). FIFTH: Predestination, the effect of which extends to each given day and is expressed in its realization in specific circumstances. All these matters are explained in more detail below.
short_answer: Five types: Eternal, Covenant, Intra-uterine, Annual, Daily.

question: What is the indication for Eternal Predestination (Al-Taqdir Al-Azali)?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'No calamity befalls on the earth or in yourselves but is inscribed in the Book of Decrees (Al-Lauh Al-Mahfuz), before We bring it into existence.' (Al-Hadid, 22). As for the Prophet (ﷺ), it is reported that he said: 'Allah wrote the destinies of His creations fifty thousand years before the creation of the heavens and the earth.' He also said: 'And His Throne was on the water.' (At-Tirmidhi, Ahmad, Abu Dawood). It is also reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Verily, the first thing Allah the Almighty created was the Pen (Al-Qalam), to which He said: "Write!" (The Pen) said: "My Lord, what shall I write?" He said: "Write the destinies of everything until the Hour is established."' (At-Tirmidhi, Ahmad, Abu Dawood). It is also reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'O Abu Hurairah, the Pen has dried concerning what will happen to you.' (Al-Bukhari, Ahmad).
short_answer: Writing by the Pen (Qalam) of the destinies of all existence before the Day of Judgment.
source: Al-Hadid, 22; Hadiths (Tirmidhi, Ahmad, Abu Dawood, Bukhari)

question: What is the indication for predestination related to life in general (Al-Taqdir Al-'Umri) and pertaining to the day of the Covenant?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'And (remember) when your Lord brought forth from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their seed (or from Adam's loin his offspring) and made them testify as to themselves (saying): "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes! We testify..."' (Al-A'raf, 172). It is narrated from Ishaq Ibn Rahwayh (may Allah be pleased with him) that a man asked the Prophet (ﷺ): "O Messenger of Allah, are deeds performed (initially by people) or were they predetermined long ago?" He replied: 'Verily, when Allah the Almighty brought forth the offspring of Adam from his loins, He made them testify as to themselves, and then He took them in His Hands and said: "These are for Paradise, and these are for the Fire." And for those who are to enter Paradise, the performance of the deeds of the people of Paradise will be facilitated, and for those who are to enter the Fire, the performance of the deeds of the people of the Fire will be facilitated.' (At-Tabarani). At-Tirmidhi cites a hadith in which Abdullah bin Amr (may Allah be pleased with both of them) said: "(Once) the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us holding two books in his hands and asked: 'Do you know what these books are?' We replied: 'No, O Messenger of Allah, unless you tell us.' Then regarding the Book that was in his right hand, he said: 'This is a Book from the Lord of the worlds, in which are recorded the names of the people of Paradise, and the names of their fathers and the names of their tribes, and they are listed there to the last one, and their number will never increase or decrease.' Then he said regarding the Book that was in his left hand: 'This is a Book from the Lord of the worlds, in which are recorded the names of the people of the Fire, and the names of their fathers and the names of their tribes, and they are listed there to the last one, and their number will never increase or decrease.' (Hearing these words,) his companions asked: 'O Messenger of Allah, if everything has already been decided, then why (strive to) perform (good) deeds?!' He said: 'Strive to do right and draw near (to perfection), for verily, he who is to enter Paradise will eventually perform the deeds of the people of Paradise, whatever he did before, and he who is to enter the Fire will eventually perform the deeds of the people of the Fire, whatever he did before.' Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a gesture with his hands and cast them (the books) away, after which he said: 'Your Lord has already decided the (destinies of His) slaves: a group (will be) in Paradise, and a group in the Fire.' (At-Tirmidhi). At-Tirmidhi, who narrated this hadith, said: 'This hadith is Hasan Sahih Gharib.'"
short_answer: The Covenant (Mithaq) with Adam's offspring and the two Books.

question: What is the indication for predestination related to a person's entire life and pertaining to the first stages of the seed in the womb?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'He knows you well when He created you from the earth (Adam), and when you were fetuses in your mothers' wombs. So ascribe not purity to yourselves. He knows best him who fears Allah and keeps his duty to Him.' (An-Najm, 32). As for the Prophet (ﷺ), it is reported that he said: 'Verily, each of you is formed in his mother's womb, remaining there for (the first) forty days (as a drop of fluid), then for the same period as a clot of blood, then for the same period as a small lump of flesh, after which an angel is sent (to him) who blows the spirit into him, and (the angel) receives a command (to record) four things, and he records his provision, his term, his deeds, and whether he will be happy or miserable. And by the One other than Whom there is no god, verily, any one of you (may) perform the deeds of the people of Paradise until he approaches Paradise to within an arm's length, (after which) what was written for him prevails, and he begins to perform the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters (the Fire). And verily, any one of you (may) perform the deeds of the people of the Fire until he approaches the Fire to within an arm's length, (after which) what was written for him prevails, and he begins to perform the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters (Paradise).' (Al-Bukhari). Other versions of this hadith are known, narrated from various companions in different wordings, but they all contain the same meaning.
short_answer: Hadith of Ibn Mas'ud about 4 things (provision, term, deeds, outcome) in the womb.

question: What is the indication for the predestination of the Night of Decree, pertaining to the events of the coming year?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'Therein (that night) is decreed every matter of ordainments. Amran (i.e. a Command or this Quran or the Decree of every matter) from Us...' (Ad-Dukhan, 4-5). It is reported that Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with both of them) said: 'On the Night of Decree, everything that will happen in the coming year relating to death, life, provision, rain, and even pilgrims is written from the Preserved Tablet, regarding whom it is said: "So-and-so will perform Hajj, so-and-so will perform Hajj."'
short_answer: Surah Ad-Dukhan, 4. Recording of deeds for the year on Laylat al-Qadr.

question: What is the indication for the existence of daily predestination?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: '...Every day He has a matter to bring forth (such as giving honor to some, disgrace to some, life to some, death to some, etc.)!' (Ar-Rahman, 29). In the "Sahih" of Al-Hakim, it is reported that Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with both of them) said: 'Verily, among what Allah the Almighty created is the Preserved Tablet (created) from a white pearl. Its cover is of red ruby, its pen is of light, and what is written in it is light. He looks into it three hundred and sixty times a day, and with each such look He creates and provides, gives life and causes death, exalts and humiliates, and He does what He wills, and this is the meaning of His words: "...Every day He has a matter to bring forth."' (Ar-Rahman, 29). All the aforementioned types of predestination are something like a detailed elaboration of the first, Eternal Predestination, which Allah the Almighty commanded the Pen to write on the Preserved Tablet when He created it. This is exactly how Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with both of them) interpreted the words of the Almighty: '...We were recording what you used to do (i.e. Our angels used to record your deeds)!' (Al-Jathiyah, 29). And the source of all this is the Knowledge of Allah, which is an attribute of the Most Glorious and Most High.
short_answer: Surah Ar-Rahman, 29. Realization of destinies daily.

question: What does the predestination of happiness and misery imply?
answer: In all the Scriptures revealed from above, as well as in the corresponding hadiths of the Prophet (ﷺ), the idea is expressed that the predestination of everything cannot serve as an obstacle to action, and does not mean that people should rely on this (and abandon action); on the contrary, it obliges them to exert all efforts for the sake of performing good deeds and striving for this. That is why when the Prophet (ﷺ) told his companions that everything is predestined, that this predestination is being fulfilled, and that the ink on the Pen with which the predestined was written has already dried, and one of them asked: "Then should we not rely on what has been predestined for us and abandon deeds?", he said in response: 'No, act, for everyone (will be) facilitated towards that for which he was created!', after which he recited the verses which say: 'As for him who gives (in charity) and keeps his duty to Allah and fears Him, and believes in Al-Husna, We will make smooth for him the path of ease (goodness). But he who is greedy miser and thinks himself self-sufficient, and belies Al-Husna, We will make smooth for him the path for evil...' (Al-Lail, 5-10). Allah the Almighty, Glory be to Him, predestined everything that is destined to be, and prepared everything that should serve as a cause for it. And He showed wisdom by granting people means for life in this world and for achieving the Hereafter, and by facilitating for every created person the performance of that for which he was created in both worlds. Thus, it is He who arranges and facilitates. And if a slave of Allah knows that the securing of his interests in the Hereafter is linked to certain means, using which he can achieve the desired goal, he will strive with all his might to resort to these means, placing them above what is related to securing his worldly interests. That companion understood this very well who, upon hearing the hadiths about predestination, said: "Now I will strive as never before!" As for the Prophet (ﷺ), it is reported that he said: 'Strive for what will benefit you, seek help from Allah, and do not lose heart.' (Muslim, Ahmad, Ibn Majah). It is also reported that when the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: "Tell me, can the medicines and incantations (Ruqyah) we resort to avert anything predestined by Allah?", he said in response: 'They (too) are part of the predestination of Allah,' meaning that Allah predestined not only good and bad, but also everything that leads to it.
short_answer: One must act, because the path is facilitated (Taysir).

question: What is the indication for the third level, that is, the obligation to believe in the Will of Allah?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'But you cannot will, unless Allah wills.' (Al-Insan, 30). 'And never say of anything, "I shall do such and such thing tomorrow." Except (with the saying), "If Allah will!"' (Al-Kahf, 23-24). 'Allah sends astray whom He wills and He guides on the Straight Path whom He wills.' (Al-An'am, 39). 'And had Allah willed, He could have made you (all) one nation.' (An-Nahl, 93). '...If Allah had willed, succeeding generations would not have fought against each other...' (Al-Baqarah, 253). '...Had it been Allah's Will, He Himself could certainly have punished them...' (Muhammad, 4). 'He does what He intends (or wills).' (Al-Buruj, 16). 'Verily, His Command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be!" and it is!' (Ya-Sin, 82). 'Verily! Our Word unto a thing when We intend it, is only that We say unto it: "Be!" and it is.' (An-Nahl, 40). Allah the Almighty also said: 'And whomsoever Allah wills to guide, He opens his breast to Islam, and whomsoever He wills to send astray, He makes his breast closed and constricted...' (Al-An'am, 125). Numerous other verses can also serve as an indication of this. As for the Prophet (ﷺ), it is reported that he said: 'Verily, the hearts of the sons of Adam are between two fingers of the Most Merciful like a single heart, and He turns it as He wills.' (Muslim). It is also reported that after he and his companions fell asleep in the valley, the Prophet (ﷺ) said about what he saw in a dream: 'Verily, Allah takes your souls when He wills and returns them when He wills.' (Al-Bukhari, An-Nasa'i, Ahmad). It is also reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Intercede (for the petitioner) and you will surely be rewarded, and Allah will decree through His Messenger what is pleasing (to Him).' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is reported that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard a man say: "As Allah wills and you will," he said (to him): 'No, as Allah alone wills!' (Ahmad). It is also reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'He for whom Allah desires good, He gives him understanding of the religion.' (Al-Bukhari, At-Tirmidhi, Ahmad). It is also reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'When Allah the Almighty wishes to show mercy to a nation, He takes its Prophet to Himself before its (disappearance) and makes him its forerunner, but if He wishes to destroy a nation, He subjects it to punishment during the lifetime of its Prophet.' (Muslim). Many other hadiths mentioning the Wish and Will of Allah can serve as examples.
short_answer: Verses and hadiths stating that everything happens by the Will and Desire of Allah.
source: Al-Insan, 30; Al-Kahf, 23-24; Al-An'am, 39, 125; An-Nahl, 40, 93; Al-Baqarah, 253; Muhammad, 4; Al-Buruj, 16; Ya-Sin, 82; Hadiths (Muslim, Bukhari, Ahmad)

question: In His Book, Allah the Almighty informed us that He loves those who do good, the pious, and the patient, which we also know from the words of His Messenger (ﷺ) and what follows from the meaning of His attributes. He is pleased with those who believe and do good deeds, He does not love the disbelievers and the unjust, He does not wish for His slaves to fall into disbelief, and He does not love corruption, but at the same time, all this exists by virtue of Allah's Wish and by His Will, and if He had willed, this would not have happened, for in His dominion there is nothing that He does not will. But what then can be answered to one who says: "How can He will and wish for that with which He is displeased and which He does not love?"
answer: Know that in various verses of the Quran and hadiths, the Will of Allah is mentioned in two senses: On the one hand, they speak of the manifestation of Allah's Will relating to existence and predestination (Irada Kawniyya), which is not always connected with love and approval, since this kind of Will includes disbelief and faith, obedience and disobedience, the beloved and the hated, and no one is able to go against it, regarding which the Almighty said: 'And whomsoever Allah wills to guide, He opens his breast to Islam, and whomsoever He wills to send astray, He makes his breast closed and constricted...' (Al-An'am, 125). Allah the Almighty also said: '...and whomsoever Allah wants to put in Al-Fitnah [error, misleading, etc.], you can do nothing for him against Allah. Those are the ones whose hearts Allah does not want to purify...' (Al-Ma'idah, 41). Other verses can serve as an indication of this. On the other hand, it refers to the manifestation of Allah's Will relating to religion and religious law (Irada Shar'iyya), which is connected with the approval and love of Allah and according to which He commanded some things and prohibited others to His slaves, and the indication of this is such words of the Almighty as: '...Allah intends for you ease, and He does not want to make things difficult for you...' (Al-Baqarah, 185). Allah the Almighty also said: 'Allah wishes to make clear (what is lawful and what is unlawful) to you, and to guide you to the ways of those who were before you, and to accept your repentance, and Allah is All-Knower, All-Wise.' (An-Nisa, 26). Other verses can serve as examples. Only he who is covered by that manifestation of His Will which relates to existence can follow this manifestation of Allah's Will (i.e., obey the religious command). In a believer who obeys Allah, both of the aforementioned manifestations are combined, but as for the wicked and rebellious person, only that manifestation of Allah's Will which relates to existence and predestination applies to him. Allah, Glory be to Him, called all His slaves to what is pleasing to Him, but He led to obedience to Himself only those of them whom He willed, as the Almighty Himself said about this: 'Allah calls to the home of peace (i.e. Paradise, by accepting Islam) and guides whom He wills to a Straight Path.' (Yunus, 25). Thus, Allah the Almighty, Glory be to Him, extends His call to all, but emphasizes that He guides only those whom He wills. Allah the Almighty said: 'Verily, your Lord is the Best Knower of him who has gone astray from His Path, and He is the Best Knower of those who are guided.' (An-Najm, 30).
short_answer: Existential Will (Kawniyya) — happens inevitably. Religious Will (Shar'iyya) — what Allah loves.
source: Al-An'am, 125; Al-Ma'idah, 41; Al-Baqarah, 185; An-Nisa, 26; Yunus, 25; An-Najm, 30

question: What are the indications for the fourth level of belief in predestination, which is related to creation?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the Wakil (Trustee, Disposer of affairs, Guardian, etc.) over all things.' (Az-Zumar, 62). 'Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the sky (rain) and the earth?' (Fatir, 3). 'This is the creation of Allah. So show Me that which those (whom you worship), besides Him have created.' (Luqman, 11). 'Allah is He Who created you, then provided food for you, then will cause you to die, then (again) He will give you life (on the Day of Resurrection). Is there any of your (so-called) partners (of Allah) that do anything of that?' (Ar-Rum, 40). 'While Allah has created you and what you do!' (As-Saffat, 96). 'And by Nafs (Adam or a person or a soul, etc.), and Him Who perfected him in proportion; Then He showed him what is wrong for him and what is right for him.' (Ash-Shams, 7-8). 'Whomsoever Allah guides, he is the guided one, and whomsoever He sends astray, those! They are the losers.' (Al-A'raf, 178). Allah the Almighty also said: '...but Allah has endeared the Faith to you and has beautified it in your hearts, and has made disbelief, wickedness and disobedience (to Allah and His Messenger) hateful to you.' (Al-Hujurat, 7). Other verses are also an indication of this. That Allah creates the actions of slaves is stated in the hadith narrated by Hudhayfah (may Allah be pleased with him), who reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Verily, Allah creates every doer and what he does.' (Al-Bukhari, Al-Bayhaqi). It is also reported that when supplicating to Allah, the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: 'O Allah! Grant my soul its piety and purify it, (for) You are the Best to purify it. You are its Guardian and Master!' (Muslim, Ahmad, An-Nasa'i (part of a long hadith)). Other hadiths are also an indication of this.
short_answer: Verses stating that Allah is the Creator of everything, including the actions of His slaves.
source: Az-Zumar, 62; Fatir, 3; Luqman, 11; Ar-Rum, 40; As-Saffat, 96; Ash-Shams, 7-8; Al-A'raf, 178; Al-Hujurat, 7; Hadiths (Bukhari, Muslim, Ahmad)

question: How should one understand the words of the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: '...all good is in Your Hands, and evil does not (come) from You...' (Al-Bukhari), considering that Allah is the Creator of everything, Glory be to Him?
answer: These words mean that all the acts of Allah the Almighty and Great are pure good in the sense that they characterize Him and proceed from Him, containing no evil. The Almighty is Wise and Just, and wisdom and justice are inherent in all His acts. The Almighty, Glory be to Him, puts everything in its place according to His Knowledge. As for the evil that befalls a person by virtue of predestination, Allah adds it to the slave as a recompense corresponding to his guilt when he begins to follow something destructive, regarding which Allah the Almighty said: 'And whatever of misfortune befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned. And He pardons much.' (Ash-Shura, 30). 'We wronged them not, but they were the Zalimun (polytheists, wrong-doers, etc.).' (Az-Zukhruf, 76). Allah the Almighty also said: 'Truly! Allah wrongs not mankind in aught; but mankind wrong themselves.' (Yunus, 44).
short_answer: Allah's Actions are good. Evil lies in the results of sins, not in the Attributes of the Creator.

question: Do the slaves of Allah possess the ability and will to perform the actions attributed to them?
answer: Yes, the slaves of Allah are capable of performing their actions and they possess desire and will. Thus, in this respect, their deeds are attributed to them justly, and in accordance with the degree of their ability, deeds are made obligatory upon them, for which they will be correspondingly rewarded or punished. Allah imposes on them only what corresponds to their capabilities. This is recorded in the Quran and Sunnah, and Allah characterized people as possessing the ability and will to perform actions, but they can do only what Allah gives them strength for, and cannot wish for anything unless Allah wills it, and they do only what Allah leads them to, as mentioned in the verses and hadiths cited above regarding Allah's Wish, Will, and creation of people's actions. They themselves do not create their actions, just as they do not create themselves. As for their ability, desire, will, and actions, all this is subordinate to the Power, Wish, and Actions of Allah, who is the Creator of themselves as well as their ability, will, desire, and actions. On the other hand, their desire, will, ability, and actions are not identical to the Wish, Will, Power, and Actions of Allah, just as they themselves are not identical to Him, for Allah is above that. On the contrary, their actions, which are created by Allah, correspond to the status of people and are justly attributed to them, being the result of Allah's deeds which correspond to His status and are justly attributed to Him, since He is actually the Doer (Creator of the act), while the slave is actually the object of the action (the acquirer). Thus, Allah, truly, is the Guide to the same extent that the slave is the guided one, and therefore both of these actions should be attributed to the One who performs them, for Allah the Almighty said: 'He whom Allah guides, he is the rightly guided one...' (Al-Isra, 97). Thus, attributing guidance (Hidaya) to Allah is lawful to the same extent as attributing to slaves that they are guided (Ihtida). On the other hand, the Guide is not identical to the guided one, just as guidance is not identical to following that guidance. And it can be said that Allah truly leads astray whom He wills, and as for the slave, he truly becomes astray. And the same can be said about all of Allah's actions towards His slaves, undertaken by Him at His discretion. If anyone attributes the action and the result of the action to the slave, it means that he has fallen into disbelief, just as he who attributes the result of the action to Allah alone has fallen into disbelief. The true believer is only he who attributes the action (creation) to the Creator, and the result of the action (performance/acquisition) to the created, since both of these statements correspond to the truth.
short_answer: Yes, but their will is subordinate to Allah's Will. Allah is the Creator, the slave is the performer (Kasib).

question: What place does belief in predestination hold in religion?
answer: Belief in predestination is the organizing principle of Monotheism (Tawhid), just as belief in the means that lead to predestined good and protect from predestined evil is the organizing principle of the Sharia. Religion can be correct and straight only for the person who believes in predestination and follows the rulings of the Sharia. An indication of this is that the Prophet (ﷺ) affirmed the obligation of belief in predestination, and when someone asked him: "Then should we not rely on what has already been written for us and abandon deeds?", he said to him in response: 'Act, for everyone is facilitated towards that for which he was created' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). Thus, he who denies predestination, claiming that it is incompatible with the Sharia, strips Allah the Almighty of such Attributes as Knowledge and Omnipotence, and declares the slave of Allah independent in his actions and the creator of those actions. This means that such a person not only claims that there is another creator alongside Allah, but claims that all created beings are creators. On the other hand, a person who acknowledges predestination but uses it as an argument against the Sharia, denying that the slave possesses the ability to perform actions and free choice with which Allah endowed him and in accordance with which He imposed certain duties on him, and claiming that Allah imposed on His slaves something beyond their power—which is like imposing on a blind person the duty to place dots over the letters in the words of the Quran—such a person attributes injustice to Allah the Almighty. His Imam in this is Iblis, may Allah curse him, for Iblis said: 'Because You have sent me astray, surely I will sit in wait against them (human beings) on Your Straight Path.' (Al-A'raf, 16). As for the true believers, they believe both in the predestination of good and evil, and that the Creator of all this is Allah; they follow the commands and prohibitions of the Sharia and refer to the Sharia for judgment secretly and openly. And they believe that only Allah can guide or lead astray, who by His Mercy leads to the Straight Path whom He wills, and whom He wills, He sends astray according to His Justice, just as they believe that He knows best in which cases one or the other is appropriate. Allah the Almighty said: 'Verily, your Lord is the Best Knower of him who has gone astray from His Path, and He is the Best Knower of those who are guided.' (An-Najm, 30). And the true believer believes that in everything related to this, Allah manifests supreme wisdom and possesses irrefutable arguments, believing also that reward and punishment depend not on predestination, but on the extent to which a person adheres to the rulings of the Sharia or neglects them. As for predestination, believers only comfort themselves with its inevitability when some misfortunes befall them. When they receive something good, they acknowledge to whom they owe it, saying: 'All the praises and thanks be to Allah, Who has guided us to this, never could we have found guidance, were it not that Allah had guided us!' (Al-A'raf, 43). And they do not repeat the words of that wicked man who said: 'This has been given to me only because of knowledge I possess.' (Al-Qasas, 78). When they commit something bad, they say the same as their parents (Adam and Eve) said: 'Our Lord! We have wronged ourselves. If You forgive us not, and bestow not upon us Your Mercy, we shall certainly be of the losers.' (Al-A'raf, 23). And they do not repeat the words of the cursed Satan, who said: 'O my Lord! Because you misled me...' (Al-Hijr, 39). If some misfortune befalls them, they say: 'Truly! To Allah we belong and truly, to Him we shall return.' (Al-Baqarah, 156). And in such cases, they do not say what the disbelievers said, about whom Allah the Almighty said: '...and say about their brothers when they travel through the earth or go out to fight: "If they had been with us, they would not have died or been killed," so that Allah may make it a cause of regret in their hearts. It is Allah that gives life and causes death. And Allah is All-Seer of what you do.' (Al Imran, 156).
short_answer: Basis of Tawhid. One must believe in Qadar and follow the Sharia.
source: Al-Bukhari, Muslim; Al-A'raf, 16, 23, 43; An-Najm, 30; Al-Qasas, 78; Al-Hijr, 39; Al-Baqarah, 156; Al Imran, 156

question: How many branches of faith are there?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'It is not Al-Birr (piety, righteousness, etc.) that you turn your faces towards east and (or) west; but Al-Birr is (the quality of) the one who believes in Allah, the Last Day, the Angels, the Book, the Prophets and gives his wealth, in spite of love for it, to the kinsfolk, to the orphans, and to Al-Masakin (the poor), and to the wayfarer, and to those who ask, and to set slaves free, performs As-Salat (Iqamat-as-Salat), and gives the Zakat, and who fulfill their covenant when they make it, and who are As-Sabirin (the patient ones, etc.) in extreme poverty and ailment (disease) and at the time of fighting (during the battles). Such are the people of the truth and they are Al-Muttaqun (pious).' (Al-Baqarah, 177). As for the Prophet (ﷺ), it is reported that he said: 'Faith (includes) more than sixty branches...' In another version of this hadith, it is reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: '...more than seventy branches, the highest of which is the saying "La ilaha illa Allah" (there is no god but Allah), and the lowest is removing something harmful from the road, and modesty is (one of) the branches of faith.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim).
short_answer: More than 60 or 70. The highest is the Shahada, the lowest is removing an obstacle.

question: How did the scholars interpret these branches?
answer: Some hadith commentators listed them, dedicating entire works to this, thereby benefiting people. However, knowing all these branches is not a necessary condition of faith: it is sufficient to believe in the existence of all of them in general, since all this is in the Quran and Sunnah. Thus, a slave should fulfill the commands of Allah and His Messenger, refrain from what they restrain him from, and believe what is reported in the Quran and Sunnah, and thanks to this he will fully satisfy the requirements of all branches of faith. As for everything listed by these people, it really relates to the deeds of faith, but to categorically assert that the meaning of the words of the Prophet (ﷺ), which the aforementioned hadith contains, consists precisely in this, appropriate indications are needed.
short_answer: Scholars listed them, but the main thing is the practice of the Quran and Sunnah.

question: What constitutes the essence of what was listed by them?
answer: In "Fath al-Bari," Ibn Hajar summarizes what Ibn Hibban said about this, saying: "Verily, these branches originate from the deeds of the heart, the deeds of the tongue, and the deeds of the body." DEEDS OF THE HEART: These are beliefs and intentions, characterized by twenty-four qualities. For example, belief in Allah implies belief in His Essence, His Attributes, and that He is the Only God, as well as that: 'There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearer, the All-Seer.' (Ash-Shura, 11). And such belief implies conviction in the createdness of everything else, as well as belief in His Angels, His Scriptures, His Messengers, the predestination of good and evil, and belief in the Last Day. Components of belief in the Last Day are belief that the deceased will be questioned in their graves, belief in the Resurrection, the Reckoning, the Scales, the Sirat, Paradise, Hell, love for Allah, love and hatred for the sake of Allah, love for the Prophet (ﷺ), and conviction that he should be honored. Components of such conviction are supplicating to Allah for the Prophet (ﷺ), following his Sunnah, and sincerity. Components of sincerity are abandoning hypocrisy and the desire to perform good deeds for show, repentance, fear, hope, gratitude, loyalty, patience, satisfaction with the predestined, reliance (Tawakkul), mercy, and humility. And finally, components of humility are showing respect to elders, compassion towards the young, as well as abandoning arrogance, vanity, envy, hatred, and anger. DEEDS OF THE TONGUE: These deeds are characterized by seven qualities, including: pronouncing the testimony of Monotheism, reciting the Quran, acquiring knowledge and transmitting it to others, supplicating to Allah (Du'a) and remembering Allah (Dhikr), which, among other things, relates to asking for forgiveness (Istighfar) and refraining from idle talk. DEEDS OF THE BODY: These deeds are characterized by thirty-eight qualities, including: - fifteen qualities concerning the person as an individual, namely - striving to maintain purity, the custom of feeding people, showing hospitality, observing obligatory and voluntary fasts, staying in the mosque for a certain time (I'tikaf), waiting for the Night of Decree, performing Hajj, Umrah, and Tawaf of the Kaaba, as well as fleeing with one's religion from temptations, which implies migrating from places where polytheism has spread, fidelity to one's vows, fulfilling oaths, and expiating for one's sins. Part of these qualities relates to those under a person's care: striving to abstain from the forbidden through marriage, observing the rights of children, showing dutifulness to parents (the latter implies refraining from disobeying them and raising children); maintaining ties of kinship. And among these qualities are those that relate to all people in general, namely: exercising just leadership, maintaining harmony among Muslims; reconciling people, helping others in acts of righteousness; and this relates to enjoining what is approved by the Sharia and forbidding what is rejected by it, and this relates to striving to maintain ties with fellow believers and returning what is entrusted; mandatory payment of debts, showing respect to the neighbor and maintaining good relationships with people; and this relates to accumulating material goods by lawful means and spending them properly; and this relates to avoiding extravagance; returning greetings, blessing the one who sneezes, ceasing to cause harm to people, refraining from vain amusements, and removing from the path what may cause harm to people.
short_answer: Deeds of the heart (24), deeds of the tongue (7), and deeds of the body (38).

question: What in the Quran and Sunnah serves as an indication of the necessity to do good (Ihsan)?
answer: There are many indications of this. For example, Allah the Almighty said: 'And do good. Truly, Allah loves Al-Muhsinun (the good-doers).' (Al-Baqarah, 195). 'Truly, Allah is with those who fear Him (keep their duty unto Him), and those who are Muhsinun (good-doers).' (An-Nahl, 128). 'And whosoever submits his face (himself) to Allah, while he is a Muhsin (good-doer), then he has grasped the most trustworthy handhold.' (Luqman, 22). 'For those who have done good is the best (reward, i.e. Paradise) and even more...' (Yunus, 26). Allah the Almighty also said: 'Is there any reward for good other than good?' (Ar-Rahman, 60). As for the Prophet (ﷺ), it is reported that he said: 'Verily, Allah has prescribed Ihsan (perfection/doing good) in everything.' (Muslim, At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah).
short_answer: Verses and hadiths about the prescription of Ihsan.
source: Al-Baqarah, 195; An-Nahl, 128; Luqman, 22; Yunus, 26; Ar-Rahman, 60; Muslim, At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah

question: What does performing worship properly (Al-Ihsan fi al-'Ibadah) imply?
answer: This concept was interpreted by the Prophet (ﷺ) himself, as reported in the hadith which tells of the questions Jibril asked the Prophet. In this hadith, it is reported that Jibril asked: "What is Ihsan (perfection)?" (The Prophet) said: '(To be perfect means) to worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then (knowing that) He, truly, sees you.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). Thus, the Prophet (ﷺ) explained that there are two types of Ihsan: 1) The highest of them is worshiping Allah as if you see Him, in other words, the station of one who seemingly sees Allah with his own eyes. This means that the slave of Allah acts as if he sees Allah the Almighty with his heart, when his heart is illuminated by the light of faith, and his mind reaches the depths of knowledge, as a result of which the hidden becomes like the obvious to him. This is the true essence of Ihsan. 2) Another type or manifestation of Ihsan is the station of a person engaged in observation (Muraqaba), when the slave of Allah clearly imagines that Allah sees him, knows about him, and is close to him. If the slave imagines all this while going about his affairs and acting accordingly, he will show sincerity towards Allah the Almighty, since this will not allow him to turn to or strive for anyone other than Allah. As for the differences between people who have reached the two stages described above, they are determined by the degree of their insight.
short_answer: To worship as if you see Allah, or knowing that He sees you.

question: What is the opposite of Faith?
answer: The opposite of Faith (Iman) is Disbelief (Kufr), which represents a foundation that, like faith, has branches. It was already stated earlier that faith is based on confirmation linked with submission, requiring the expression of obedience in the form of fulfilling religious duties. As for disbelief, it is based on denial and obstinacy, inevitably linked with arrogance and disobedience. All religious duties belong to one or another branch of faith, and in some verses and hadiths, as we noted earlier, many of these duties were explicitly called faith. On the other hand, all sins belong to one or another branch of disbelief, and in some verses and hadiths, many of them were explicitly called disbelief, which we will talk about in more detail below. Thus, if you know this, then you know that disbelief is of two types: Major Disbelief (Al-Kufr Al-Akbar), which completely places a person outside the fold of faith. This kind of disbelief is related to beliefs incompatible with words, or deeds of the heart, or with any one of these. Minor Disbelief (Al-Kufr Al-Asghar), which is incompatible with the perfection of faith, but does not absolutely contradict faith. This kind of disbelief finds its expression in deeds, but does not contradict either words or deeds of the heart and does not necessarily require this.
short_answer: Kufr (Disbelief).

question: Why is disbelief in belief completely incompatible with faith? How can it be explained in more detail why such disbelief leads to the disappearance of faith?
answer: It has already been said that faith is a combination of word and deed. This refers to the words of the heart and tongue and the deeds of the heart, tongue, and other parts of the body. By words of the heart is meant conviction, and by words of the tongue is meant the pronunciation of the words of the testimony of Monotheism. As for the deeds of the heart, they mean intentions and the manifestation of sincerity, whereas deeds of the parts of the body mean obedience, finding its expression in the fulfillment of all religious duties. Thus, with the cessation of the words and deeds of the heart, the words of the tongue, and the deeds performed by various parts of the body, faith disappears completely; if the conviction of the heart disappears, then everything else becomes useless. The conviction of the heart is a necessary condition for the validity of the aforementioned four conditions and their usefulness, as in the case of those who do not believe in the Names and Attributes of Allah or in anything of what Allah sent His Messengers with and what He revealed in His Scriptures. All adherents of the Sunnah are unanimous in the opinion that if the deeds of the heart cease, this leads to the complete disappearance of faith, even if sincere conviction remains. And they all believe that the conviction of the heart alone is useless if it is not supported by deeds which are the expression of its love and obedience. Thus, neither Iblis, nor Pharaoh, nor his people, nor the polytheists, nor the followers of other religions who were convinced of the truthfulness of the Messengers and confirmed it secretly and openly, received any benefit, but at the same time said: "He is not a liar, but we will not follow him and will not believe in him!"
short_answer: Without the conviction of the heart and submission, faith is invalid.
source: Explanation of the Essence of Faith

question: Into how many parts is Major Disbelief (Al-Kufr Al-Akbar), which puts a person outside the fold of religion, divided?
answer: From all that we have already said, it follows that it consists of four parts: disbelief expressed in the form of ignorance (Jahl) and denial (Takdhib), disbelief expressed in the form of refusal/rejection (Juhud), disbelief expressed in the form of obstinacy ('Inad) and showing arrogance (Istikbar), and disbelief expressed in the form of hypocrisy (Nifaq).
short_answer: Four: Takdhib, Juhud, 'Inad, Nifaq.

question: What exactly constitutes disbelief expressed in the form of ignorance and denial?
answer: This kind of disbelief can manifest itself both outwardly and inwardly, an example of which is the behavior of the majority of the disbelieving Quraish and those who lived before them, about whom Allah the Almighty said: '...Those who deny the Book (this Quran), and that with which We sent Our Messengers (i.e. to worship none but Allah Alone sincerely, and to reject all false deities, etc.). But they will come to know.' (Ghafir, 70). '...and turn away from Al-Jahilun (the ignorant).' (Al-A'raf, 199). 'And (remember) the Day when We shall gather out of every nation a troop of those who denied Our Ayat (proofs, evidences, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.), and they (all) shall be gathered (and driven to the place of reckoning), till, when they come (before their Lord at the place of reckoning), He will say: "Did you deny My Ayat whereas you comprehended them not by knowledge (that they were the truth), or what was it that you used to do?"' (An-Naml, 83-84). Allah the Almighty also said: 'Nay, they deny that; the knowledge whereof they could not compass and whereof the interpretation has not yet come unto them.' (Yunus, 39). Other verses can also serve as an indication of this.
short_answer: Considering the truth to be a lie (example of the Quraish).

question: What exactly constitutes disbelief expressed in the form of refusal (Juhud)?
answer: In this case, it refers to the concealment of the truth and outward disobedience to it by those who acknowledge it inwardly. An example of such disbelief is the disbelief of Pharaoh and his people in Musa and the disbelief of the Jews in Muhammad (ﷺ). Regarding the disbelief of Pharaoh and his people, Allah the Almighty said: 'And they belied them (those Ayat) wrongfully and arrogantly...' (An-Naml, 14). As for the Jews, the Almighty said about them: '...then when there came to them that which they had recognized, they disbelieved in it.' (Al-Baqarah, 89). Allah the Almighty also said: '...Verily, a party of them conceal the truth while they know it.' (Al-Baqarah, 146).
short_answer: Rejection of the truth despite knowing it inwardly (Pharaoh, Jews).

question: What exactly constitutes disbelief expressed in the form of obstinacy and showing arrogance?
answer: In this case, it refers to disobedience to the truth combined with an internal acknowledgment of it, an example of which is the disbelief of Iblis, about which Allah the Almighty said: 'And (remember) when We said to the angels: "Prostrate yourselves before Adam." And they prostrated except Iblis (Satan), he refused and was proud and was one of the disbelievers (disobedient to Allah).' (Al-Baqarah, 34). Iblis could not deny the very fact of Allah's command to bow down before Adam, just as he could not deny that he received such a command, but nevertheless he began to object to this command and defame the wisdom and justice of the One who gave it, saying, as Allah the Almighty informed us: 'Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?' (Al-Isra, 61). Allah the Almighty also informed that he said: 'I am not the one to prostrate myself to a human being, whom You created from dried (sounding) clay of altered mud.' (Al-Hijr, 33). And Allah the Almighty informed that Iblis said: 'I am better than him (Adam), You created me from fire, and him You created from clay.' (Al-A'raf, 12).
short_answer: Disobedience to the truth despite acknowledging it (Iblis).

question: What exactly constitutes disbelief expressed in the form of hypocrisy?
answer: In this case, it refers to the absence of conviction of the heart and its inaction, combined with an external expression of obedience, which is done for show to people. Such was the disbelief of Ibn Salul and his henchmen, about whom Allah the Almighty said: 'And of mankind, there are some (hypocrites) who say: "We believe in Allah and the Last Day" while in fact they believe not. They (think to) deceive Allah and those who believe, while they only deceive themselves, and perceive (it) not! In their hearts is a disease (of doubt and hypocrisy) and Allah has increased their disease. A painful torment is theirs because they used to tell lies. And when it is said to them: "Make not mischief on the earth," they say: "We are only peacemakers." Verily! They are the ones who make mischief, but they perceive not. And when it is said to them (hypocrites): "Believe as the people (followers of Muhammad Peace be upon him , Al-Ansar and Al-Muhajirun) have believed," they say: "Shall we believe as the fools have believed?" Verily, they are the fools, but they know not. And when they meet those who believe, they say: "We believe," but when they are alone with their Shayatin (devils - polytheists, hypocrites, etc.), they say: "Truly, we are with you; verily, we were but mocking." Allah mocks at them and gives them increase in their wrong-doings to wander blindly. These are they who have purchased error for guidance, so their commerce was profitless. And they were not guided. Their likeness is as the likeness of one who kindled a fire; then, when it lighted all around him, Allah took away their light and left them in darkness. (So) they could not see. They are deaf, dumb, and blind, so they return not (to the Right Path). Or like a rainstorm from the sky, wherein is darkness, thunder, and lightning. They thrust their fingers in their ears to keep out the stunning thunderclap for fear of death. But Allah ever encompasses the disbelievers (i.e. Allah will gather them all together). The lightning almost snatches away their sight, whenever it flashes for them, they walk therein, and when darkness covers them, they stand still. And if Allah willed, He could have taken away their hearing and their sight. Certainly, Allah has power over all things.' (Al-Baqarah, 8-20).
short_answer: External obedience with absence of faith in the heart (Nifaq).

question: What constitutes disbelief manifested in deeds, but not placing a person outside the fold of religion?
answer: The manifestation of such disbelief is any sin that is called disbelief in the Quran and Sunnah, although the one who commits it continues to be called a believer. An example is the words of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: 'Do not become disbelievers after me, striking each other's necks.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is also reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Abusing a Muslim is Fusuq (evil-doing/sin) and killing him is Kufr (disbelief).' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). Thus, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called Muslims fighting each other disbelief, and those who engage in it disbelievers. Furthermore, Allah the Almighty said: 'And if two parties or groups among the believers fall to fighting, then make peace between them both, but if one of them rebels against the other, then fight you (all) against the one that which rebels till it complies with the Command of Allah; then if it complies, then make reconciliation between them justly, and be equitable. Verily! Allah loves those who are equitable. The believers are nothing else than brothers (in Islamic religion). So make reconciliation between your brothers, and fear Allah, that you may receive mercy.' (Al-Hujurat, 9-10). Thus, Allah the Almighty confirms that they possess faith and are brothers in faith, without denying this in the slightest. And in the verse about equal retribution (Qisas), Allah the Almighty says: 'But if the killer is forgiven by the brother (or the relatives, etc.) of the killed against blood money, then adhering to it with fairness and payment of the blood money, to the heir should be made in fairness.' (Al-Baqarah, 178). Thus, here too Allah the Almighty confirms the killer's belonging to the brotherhood in Islam, without denying it. In addition, it is reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'The adulterer is not a believer while he is committing adultery, and the thief is not a believer while he is stealing, and the person who drinks wine is not a believer while he is drinking it, but after (committing such things) repentance is offered.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). In another version of this hadith, it is reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) also said: '...and the killer is not a believer when he kills.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). In the third version of this hadith, it is reported that the Prophet also said: '...and when a robber forcibly takes something in front of people, he is not a believer.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). All of the above indicates that the Prophet (ﷺ) did not consider that the adulterer, thief, wine-drinker, and killer completely lose faith, provided they profess Monotheism. And if he had wanted to say something like that, he would not have reported that the deceased who does not abandon the testimony of Monotheism until death will enter Paradise, even if he committed the aforementioned sins, for only believers will enter Paradise. Thus, speaking about this, the Prophet (ﷺ) only wanted to point out the decrease of such a person's faith and its imperfection. As for disbelief, a slave of Allah falls into it if he commits the aforementioned sins believing that he is allowed to do so, since this means that he considers incorrect those parts of the Quran and Sunnah where the prohibition of such things is indicated. He also becomes a disbeliever if he only considers it permissible, even without doing anything of the sort, and Allah the Almighty knows best.
short_answer: Major sins named 'Kufr' but not expelling one from religion.

question: Previously, disbelief manifested in actions was defined as minor disbelief, but why then does prostrating to idols, showing disrespect to the Quran, reviling the Messenger, mocking religion, and similar things place a person outside of religion?
answer: Know that the four aforementioned and similar actions are a manifestation of disbelief finding its expression in deeds only in the sense that they are performed with the help of various parts of the body, and people can see this. However, their performance can take place only when the deeds of the heart related to intentions, sincerity, love, and obedience completely cease. Thus, despite the fact that outwardly all these actions are manifestations of disbelief finding expression in deeds, they are necessarily connected with disbelief related to beliefs, and can be performed either by a hypocrite who has deviated from the true path or by a stubborn sinner. And only this, during the campaign to Tabuk, forced the hypocrites to do what is said in the Quran: '...they uttered the word of disbelief, and they disbelieved after their Islam, and they planned that which they could not attain...' (At-Tawbah, 74). And in the Quran it is also reported about them: 'If you ask them (about this), they declare: "We were only talking idly and joking." Say: "Was it at Allah, and His Ayat (proofs, evidences, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.) and His Messenger that you were mocking?" Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after you had believed.' (At-Tawbah, 65-66). Moreover, we did not define minor disbelief exclusively as disbelief finding its expression in deeds, but said that it is such if it does not relate to beliefs and does not contradict either the words or deeds of the heart.
short_answer: Mockery is a sign of the absence of faith in the heart (Major Kufr).

question: Into how many parts are such things as injustice (Zulm), wickedness (Fusuq), and hypocrisy (Nifaq) divided?
answer: Each of these things is divided into two parts: major, which is disbelief, and minor, which is everything that is less than disbelief.
short_answer: Into two: Major (Kufr) and Minor (Sin).

question: What can serve as an example of major and minor injustice?
answer: An example of major injustice is what Allah the Almighty mentions when He says: 'And do not invoke besides Allah that which neither benefits you nor harms you, for if you do so, then indeed you would be among the wrongdoers.' (Yunus, 106). 'Indeed, associating others with Allah is a tremendous injustice!' (Luqman, 13). 'Indeed, Allah has made Paradise forbidden for those who worship others alongside Him, and their refuge will be the Fire, and the wrongdoers will have no helpers!' (Al-Ma'idah, 72). As for injustice that is lesser than this, an example can be found in what Allah the Almighty mentions in Surah At-Talaq when He says: '...and fear Allah, your Lord. Do not expel them from their houses, nor should they leave unless they commit a clear immorality. These are the limits of Allah, and whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has certainly wronged himself.' (At-Talaq, 1). Allah the Almighty also says: '...and do not retain them to harm them and transgress, and whoever does that has certainly wronged himself.' (Al-Baqarah, 231).
short_answer: Major — Shirk (polytheism). Minor — violation of rights and sins.

question: What can serve as an example of major and minor wickedness?
answer: An example of major wickedness is what Allah the Almighty mentions when He says: 'Indeed, the hypocrites are the wicked ones.' (At-Tawbah, 67).
