'...except Iblis, who was of the jinn and departed from the command of his Lord.' (Al-Kahf, 50). 'And to Lot We gave judgment and knowledge and saved him from the town that practiced wicked deeds. Indeed, they were an evil and wickedly defiant people.' (Al-Anbiya, 74). As for wickedness that is lesser than this, an example is what Allah the Almighty said about slanderers: '...and never accept their testimony, for they are the wicked ones.' (An-Nur, 4). Allah the Almighty also says: 'O you who have believed, if a wicked person brings you news, investigate it, lest you harm people out of ignorance and then become regretful for what you have done.' (Al-Hujurat, 6). It is reported that this verse was revealed concerning Al-Walid bin Uqbah.
short_answer: Major — leaving Islam (Iblis). Minor — sins (slander).

question: What can serve as an example of major and minor hypocrisy?
answer: Examples of major hypocrisy are given in the verses we quoted from the beginning of Surah Al-Baqarah. Allah the Almighty also says: 'Indeed, the hypocrites think they deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them! And when they stand for prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to people and only remembering Allah a little. Wavering between them, neither to these nor to those. And whoever Allah leaves astray, you will never find for him a way. O you who have believed, do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers. Do you wish to give Allah a clear case against yourselves? Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, and you will never find for them a helper.' (An-Nisa, 142-145). Allah the Almighty also says: 'When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We testify that you are the Messenger of Allah." And Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars.' (Al-Munafiqun, 1). Other verses can also serve as examples. As for hypocrisy that is lesser than this, an example is what the Prophet ﷺ mentioned when he said: 'The hypocrite has three signs: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks it; and when he is entrusted, he betrays.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is also reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'A true hypocrite is one who possesses four characteristics, and whoever has one of them has a characteristic of hypocrisy until he abandons it: he betrays when entrusted, he lies when he speaks, he acts treacherously when making agreements, and he transgresses when he disputes.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim).
short_answer: Major — in faith (takes one out of Islam). Minor — in deeds (lying, betrayal).

question: What are the Sharia rulings regarding magic and magicians?
answer: Magic truly exists, and as for its effect, it is nothing more than coinciding with what is predestined, as Allah the Almighty indicated when He said: 'And they learned from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife. But they do not harm anyone through it except by permission of Allah.' (Al-Baqarah, 102). The effect of magic is also mentioned in authentic hadiths. As for the magician, he is a disbeliever if he acquires his magical skills from devils, as mentioned in the aforementioned verse from Surah Al-Baqarah, for Allah the Almighty said: 'Neither of them would teach anyone until they said, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve." But they learned from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife. But they do not harm anyone through it except by permission of Allah. And they learn what harms them and does not benefit them. And they certainly knew that whoever purchased it would have no share in the Hereafter.' (Al-Baqarah, 102).
short_answer: Magic is forbidden, the magician is a disbeliever (Kafir).

question: What is 'nushrah' and what are the Sharia rulings regarding it?
answer: This refers to removing magic spells from the bewitched person. If it is done through similar magic, it belongs to the works of Satan. But if it is done through lawful Quranic incantations, there is nothing wrong with it.
short_answer: Removing spells. Permitted with Quran (Ruqyah), forbidden with magic.

question: What are lawful and forbidden incantations (ruqyah)?
answer: Lawful incantations are words taken only from the Quran or Sunnah, recited in Arabic, where both the one performing the incantation and the one being treated believe that these words can only have effect with Allah's permission, the Almighty and Great. For example, the Prophet ﷺ was treated with incantations by Jibril (peace be upon him), and he himself treated many of his companions, not only permitting this for them but also commanding them to engage in such incantations, allowing them to take payment for it, as reported in hadiths found in both Sahihs and many other sources. Forbidden are all those that are not related to the Quran and Sunnah and are not recited in Arabic. Such practices belong to the works of Satan, using him and drawing near to him through what he loves, which is what many deceivers, charlatans, and deranged people engage in, as well as many who read books dealing with various symbols and talismans allegedly capable of protecting people, which were compiled by enemies of Islam and have no relation to true Islam.
short_answer: Lawful — from Quran/Sunnah. Forbidden — incomprehensible words, shirk.

question: What are the Sharia rulings regarding various items hung in different places like amulets, tendons, rings, threads, shells and similar objects?
answer: It is reported that during one of his journeys, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a messenger ahead to warn people not to leave tendon necklaces or any similar items on the necks of camels, but to cut them off. It is also reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Indeed, incantations, amulets, and love spells are shirk (polytheism).' (Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, Ahmad). It is also reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever hangs an amulet has committed shirk.' (Ahmad). It is reported that once the Prophet ﷺ saw a copper ring on someone's hand and asked him: 'What is this?' The man said: 'It is for weakness,' and then the Prophet ﷺ commanded: 'Indeed, it will only increase your weakness, throw it away, for if you die without removing it, you will never succeed.' (Al-Hakim, Ahmad). It is reported that once Hudhayfah (may Allah be pleased with him) cut a thread that a man had wrapped around his arm, then recited the following verse: 'And most of them believe not in Allah except while they associate others with Him.' (Yusuf, 106).
short_answer: Forbidden, this is Shirk (polytheism).

question: What can be said about fortune-tellers (kuhhan)?
answer: Fortune-tellers are among the taghut and are friends of the devils who whisper to them, as Allah the Almighty said: 'And indeed, the devils inspire their allies...' (Al-An'am, 121). Devils descend to them, conveying words they overhear from angels' conversations, while fortune-tellers add a hundred lies to one word of truth, about which Allah the Almighty said: 'Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend? They descend upon every sinful liar. They pass on what they hear, and most of them are liars.' (Ash-Shu'ara, 221-223). As for the Prophet ﷺ, in the hadith about revelation it is reported that he said: 'And the eavesdroppers listen to them, positioned one above another. Each one hears something and passes the overheard words to the one below him, who passes them to another positioned even lower, and this continues until one of them conveys them to a sorcerer or fortune-teller. Sometimes a shooting star strikes him before he can convey these words, and sometimes he conveys them before it strikes him, and along with one word of truth he conveys a hundred lies.' (Al-Bukhari, Ibn Majah - part of a long hadith). The same applies to things like divination in sand, divination with pebbles, etc.
short_answer: Liars collaborating with devils.

question: What judgment should be made about one who believes a fortune-teller?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'Say, "None in the heavens and earth knows the unseen except Allah."' (An-Naml, 65). 'And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him.' (Al-An'am, 59). 'Or do they have knowledge of the unseen, so they write it down?' (Al-Qalam, 47). 'Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so he sees?' (An-Najm, 35). Allah the Almighty also said: '...Allah knows, while you do not know.' (Al-Baqarah, 216). As for the Prophet ﷺ, it is reported that he said: 'Whoever comes to a diviner or fortune-teller and believes what he says has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad ﷺ.' (Abu Dawud, Ahmad, Al-Hakim). It is also reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever comes to a fortune-teller and asks him about something, his prayer will not be accepted for forty days.' (Muslim, Ahmad).
short_answer: To believe is Kufr. To ask is a sin (no prayer for 40 days).
source: Quran (verses about Ghayb); Hadiths (Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Muslim)

question: What judgment should be made about astrology?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'And He is the One who created the stars for you so that you may be guided by them through the darkness of land and sea...' (Al-An'am, 97). 'And We have adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and made them as missiles against the devils...' (Al-Mulk, 5). Allah the Almighty also said: '...and the stars are subjected by His command...' (An-Nahl, 12). As for the Prophet ﷺ, it is reported that he said: 'Whoever engages in any type of astrology has engaged in a type of magic, and the more he learns of it, the deeper he becomes in magic.' (Abu Dawud, Ahmad, Ibn Majah). It is reported that Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said about people who wrote 'Abajad' and looked at stars: 'I do not think that one who does this will have any share with Allah.' It is narrated that Qatadah (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Allah created these stars for three purposes: to adorn the heavens, as missiles against devils, and as signs by which people can find their way. If anyone sees anything else in them, he does so to his own misfortune, destroys his own portion, and takes on what he has no knowledge of.'
short_answer: It is a type of magic (Sihr) and is forbidden.
source: Al-An'am, 97; Al-Mulk, 5; An-Nahl, 12; Hadith (Abu Dawud); Qatadah

question: What can be said about seeking rain from celestial bodies?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'And you make your provision that you deny.' (Al-Waqi'ah, 82). As for the Prophet ﷺ, it is reported that he said: 'Four things from the time of ignorance that members of my ummah still cannot give up: boasting about noble lineage, defaming others for their ancestry, seeking rain from celestial bodies, and wailing loudly over the dead.' (Muslim, At-Tirmidhi). It is also reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Do you know what your Lord said?' They said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' Then the Prophet ﷺ said that Allah the Almighty said: 'This morning some of My servants remained believers in Me, while some became disbelievers. As for the one who said: "We were given rain by the mercy and compassion of Allah," he believes in Me and does not believe in planets. But as for the one who said: "We were given rain because of such-and-such planet," he does not believe in Me and believes in planets.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim).
short_answer: This is Kufr (disbelief) in Allah and shirk.

question: What can be said about belief in bad omens and what removes it?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'Indeed, their misfortune is with Allah, but most of them do not know.' (Al-A'raf, 131). As for the Prophet ﷺ, it is reported that he said: 'There is no contagion except by Allah's will, nor is the flight of birds a bad omen, nor is the owl, nor is the month of Safar...' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is also reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Belief in bad omens is shirk, belief in bad omens is shirk!' (Ahmad, Al-Hakim, At-Tirmidhi). As for Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), it is reported that he said: 'There is none among us who does not have some of this, but Allah removes it through reliance.' It is narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr (may Allah be pleased with him) that once the Prophet ﷺ said: 'A person who is kept from doing what he needs to do because of a bad omen has fallen into shirk.' People asked: 'What is the expiation for this?' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The expiation is to say: "O Allah, there is no good except Your good, no birds except Your birds, and there is no god but You!"' (Ahmad). It is also reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'The best thing is a good omen, and let not the bad omen stop a Muslim. If one of you sees something he dislikes, let him say: "O Allah, none brings good things except You, and none repels bad things except You, and there is no power or strength except with You."' (Abu Dawud).
short_answer: This is Shirk. Removed by reliance (tawakkul) and dua.
source: Al-A'raf, 131; Hadiths (Bukhari, Muslim, Ahmad, Abu Dawud)

question: What can be said about the evil eye?
answer: It is reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'The evil eye is real.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is also reported that once, seeing a dark spot on the face of a slave girl, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Treat her with ruqyah, for indeed, she has been afflicted by the evil eye.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is narrated that Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: 'The Prophet ﷺ commanded me (or: ...commanded) to treat with ruqyah against the evil eye.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is also reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'There should be no ruqyah except for the evil eye and poison.' (Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi, Ahmad). This is also mentioned in many other authentic hadiths that we have not cited, the meaning of which is that all this has an effect only by Allah's permission, and many of our righteous predecessors (may Allah be pleased with them) used these hadiths in interpreting the words of the Almighty and Great Allah when He said: 'And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes when they hear the message...' (Al-Qalam, 51).
short_answer: Evil eye is real. Treated with lawful Ruqyah.

question: How many types of sins exist?
answer: Sins are divided into minor ones (sagha'ir), also called bad deeds (sayyiat), and major ones (kaba'ir), also called mortal sins (mubikat).
short_answer: Two types: Minor (Saghair) and Major (Kabair).

question: How are bad deeds (sayyiat) expiated?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will expiate from you your minor sins and admit you through a noble entrance.' (An-Nisa, 31). Allah the Almighty also said: 'Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds.' (Hud, 114). Thus, Allah the Almighty informed us that bad deeds are expiated by avoiding major sins and performing good deeds. The same idea is expressed in the hadith where it is reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: '...after doing something bad, do something good that will erase it...' (Ahmad, At-Tirmidhi). Additionally, in other authentic hadiths it is reported that expiation for various bad deeds and minor sins is achieved through things such as performing ablution properly despite disliking aspects of it, going to the mosque, performing the five daily prayers, regularly attending Friday prayers, fasting in Ramadan, performing additional prayers during Ramadan, worshiping Allah on the Night of Decree, fasting on the Day of Ashura, and fulfilling other religious obligations. In most of these hadiths, the possibility of such expiation is conditional on not committing major sins, and hadiths that do not mention any conditions also encourage this. Thus, avoiding major sins is a necessary condition for expiating minor sins through good deeds, as well as without them.
short_answer: By avoiding major sins and performing good deeds.

question: Which sins are among the major ones?
answer: The criterion for determining major sins comes from statements of the Prophet's companions ﷺ, their followers, and some other individuals. Some said that a major sin is any sin for which punishment is specified in the Quran. Others claimed it is every sin that entails curse or Allah's anger, leads to Hell or other punishment. Still others believed it is every sin that indicates that the one committing it does not pay attention to religion, does not heed it, and does not have great fear of Allah. Other opinions were also expressed. As for authentic hadiths, many transgressions are called major in them, despite differences in their degrees. Among them are major disbelief, manifestations of which include polytheism and magic. They also include other great sins, though less severe, such as killing a person whom Allah has forbidden to kill except by right, fleeing from battle, usury, appropriating orphan's property, uttering false words, slandering chaste believing women who are not cautious enough, drinking wine, showing disobedience and disrespect toward parents, and a number of other transgressions, about which Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: 'Their number is closer to seventy than to seven.' One who undertakes to count the number of sins called major will see that there are actually more than seventy, but what would happen if someone undertook to count all those sins after the mention of which in the Quran and Sunnah terrible threats follow, connected with curses, manifestations of Allah's anger, torments, or other things? Such a person would certainly discover that the number of such sins is very large.
short_answer: Sins with hadd (punishment) or threat of Hell/anger. About 70.

question: How can all minor and major sins be expiated?
answer: All of them can be expiated through sincere repentance. Allah the Almighty said: 'O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance. Perhaps your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow.' (At-Tahrim, 8). '...except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous work. For them Allah will replace their evil deeds with good ones...' (Al-Furqan, 70). Allah the Almighty also said: 'And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins - and who can forgive sins except Allah? - and do not persist in what they were doing while they know. Those - their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow...' (Al Imran, 135-136). Other verses can serve as examples. As for the Prophet ﷺ, it is reported that he said: 'Indeed, Allah rejoices at the repentance of His servant more than a man who stops in a dangerous place with his she-camel on which his food and water are loaded. This man lays his head on something and sleeps for a short time, and when he wakes up, he sees that his she-camel has disappeared, and he is already tormented by heat, thirst, and whatever else Allah wills, and then he says: "I will return to my previous place," and he returns to it, sleeps for a short time, and when he raises his head, it turns out that his she-camel is standing nearby.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim).
short_answer: Only through sincere repentance (Tawbah).
source: At-Tahrim, 8; Al-Furqan, 70; Al Imran, 135-136; Hadiths (Bukhari, Muslim)

question: What is sincere repentance (at-tawbah an-nasuh)?
answer: This refers to heartfelt repentance that combines three things: 1 - Ceasing the commission of this sin. 2 - Regret for having committed this sin. 3 - Determination never to return to it. Moreover, if committing this sin involves harming another Muslim, it is necessary to free oneself from this as much as possible, because otherwise the offended party will demand compensation on the Day of Resurrection and will certainly achieve retribution with equal measure, as this relates to such injustices that Allah does not forgive in anything. It is reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'If a person has anything unjustly appropriated belonging to his brother, let him free himself from it today, for in the eternal world there will be neither dinars nor dirhams, and therefore this must be done before his good deeds are taken from him and given to his brother. But if he has no good deeds, then his brother's bad deeds will be taken and thrown upon him.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim).
short_answer: Cessation, regret, determination not to repeat (+ return of rights).

question: When will repentance cease to be accepted for each individual?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'Indeed, Allah accepts the repentance of those who commit evil in ignorance and then repent soon after. It is those to whom Allah will turn in forgiveness, and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise!' (An-Nisa, 17). All the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ agreed that any act expressing disobedience to Allah is committed in ignorance, regardless of whether it is done intentionally or not. And all of them believed that the word 'soon' indicates any moment in time before a person's death hour comes. It is reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Indeed, Allah will accept the repentance of His servant as long as his death rattle has not begun.' (At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Ahmad, Al-Hakim). The same idea is expressed in many other hadiths. But if a person has already seen the angel of death, and begins to make a death rattle and his soul rises to his throat, then after this repentance will no longer be accepted and there will be no deliverance then, for Allah the Almighty said: 'How many generations have We destroyed before them! And they cried out, but it was already too late to escape.' (Sad, 3). And the Almighty and Great also said what is directly related to His previous words: 'And repentance is not accepted of those who commit evil all their lives, and when death comes to one of them, he says: "Indeed, now I repent!"' (An-Nisa, 18).
short_answer: At the moment of death rattle (Gharghara).

question: When will repentance cease to be accepted in earthly life?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'On the Day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith as long as it had not believed before or had not earned through its faith some good.' (Al-An'am, 158). As for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, it is reported that he said: 'The Hour will not come until the sun rises from the west, and when it rises from there and people see it, all of them will believe, but this will happen at a time when a person's faith will not benefit him,' - after which he recited the aforementioned verse. And many other hadiths are known, transmitted from different companions of the Prophet ﷺ, having the same meaning. For example, Safwan bin Assal (may Allah be pleased with him) transmitted that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Indeed, the Almighty and Great Allah has opened in the west a gate of repentance seventy years' journey wide, and it will not be closed until the sun rises from there.' (At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Ahmad).
short_answer: After the sun rises from the west.

question: What can be said about a person who professes Tawhid but dies persisting in major sins?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'And We shall set up scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be treated unjustly at all. And if there be the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth, and sufficient are We as Reckoners.' (Al-Anbiya, 47). 'The weighing on that Day will be true. Those whose scales are heavy - they will be successful. As for those whose scales are light, they have lost their souls for disregarding Our signs.' (Al-A'raf, 8-9). 'On that Day when every soul will find present what it has done of good and what it has done of evil...' (Al Imran, 30). 'On that Day when every soul will come disputing for itself, and every soul will be fully compensated for what it did, and they will not be wronged.' (An-Nahl, 111). 'And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah. Then every soul will be compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.' (Al-Baqarah, 281). Allah the Almighty also said: 'On that Day, people will come forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds. So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.' (Az-Zalzalah, 6-8). Other verses can also serve as examples. It is reported that when the Prophet ﷺ said: 'One who is called to full account will be punished,' Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) asked: 'Doesn't Allah the Almighty say: "...he will be judged with an easy account..."' (Al-Inshiqaq, 8). The Prophet ﷺ said: 'This refers only to the presentation, but one who is called to full account will be punished.' (Al-Bukhari, At-Tirmidhi, Ahmad). Previously we already cited Quranic verses and hadiths that speak about the gathering of people on the Day of Resurrection, their situation during the waiting period for Judgment, the Scales, the unfolding of scrolls with records of their deeds, the presentation of these deeds for Judgment, the reckoning, the Sirat, types of intercession, and other matters. Through this, differences in the degrees of people and their position in the eternal world will become known, which will be determined by the degree of their obedience or disobedience to their Lord in this world, and that among them are those who are foremost, moderate, and those who wrong themselves. If you understand this, then know that based on what is stated in the verses of the Quran and hadiths comprising the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ, and what our righteous predecessors followed - the Companions who constituted the first generation of Islam and those who followed them with pure hearts, including the best interpreters of the Quran and scholars of the Sunnah - sinners from among those who profess the religion of Tawhid are divided into three categories. FIRST: those whose good deeds outweigh the bad - they will enter Paradise, and the Fire will never touch them. SECOND: those whose good deeds are equal in quantity to the bad, so their bad deeds will not allow them to enter Paradise, while their good deeds will protect them from the Fire. These people will be on the Heights (Al-A'raf), and speaking of them, Allah the Almighty mentioned that they will be detained between Paradise and Hell for as long as Allah wills, after which they will be allowed to enter Paradise. Allah the Almighty said about this, after informing that the inhabitants of Paradise will enter Paradise and the inhabitants of the Fire will be in the Fire, and then these people will call out to both groups. Allah the Almighty said: 'And between them will be a partition, and on the Heights are men who recognize all by their mark. They will call out to the companions of Paradise, "Peace be upon you." They have not entered it, but they aspire to it. And when their eyes are turned toward the companions of the Fire, they say, "Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people." And those on the Heights will call to men they recognize by their marks, saying, "Of no avail to you was your gathering and your arrogance. Are these not the ones whom you swore that Allah would never grant them mercy? [To them Allah will say], "Enter Paradise; no fear shall come upon you, nor shall you grieve."' (Al-A'raf, 46-49). THIRD: people who will meet Allah without ceasing to commit major sins and indulging in debauchery, but at the same time they will continue to adhere to the religion of Tawhid and maintain faith. Their bad deeds will outweigh the good, and they will enter the Fire according to their sins: among them will be those for whom the Fire will reach their ankles, those whom it will engulf up to mid-shin, those for whom it will reach the knees, and even those who will be completely engulfed by Fire, except for the traces of prostration, which Allah will forbid the Fire to touch. For those people who belong to this category, Allah the Almighty will permit our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to intercede, and after him - other prophets, the righteous, angels, and those whom He wishes to honor by granting them the right of intercession. And He will set a certain limit for them, and they will begin to bring them out, after which He will again set a certain limit for them, and they will again bring them out of the Fire. First, they will bring out those who have good (khayr) in their hearts weighing a dinar, then those who have good weighing half a dinar, then those who have good weighing a grain of wheat, and this will continue until they bring out those who have good in their hearts weighing at least a speck of dust or even less. After this, these intercessors will say: 'Our Lord, we have not left any good there!' - and no one who died professing the religion of Tawhid will remain in the Fire forever, regardless of what their deeds were. The greater the faith of such people and the lighter their transgressions, the lighter the torments in the flames of Hell they will undergo, the less time they will stay there, and the sooner they will leave it. Conversely, the heavier their sins and the weaker their faith, the heavier and longer the torments they will experience. This is mentioned in a great multitude of hadiths, and the Prophet ﷺ indicated this when he said: 'The one who says "There is no god but Allah" will benefit from these words one day, even if this happens after he has been punished.' (Al-Haythami). In general, this is a difficult and dangerous topic about which different opinions have been expressed, and Allah the Almighty said: 'But Allah guided those who believed to the truth concerning that over which they had differed, by His permission. And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.' (Al-Baqarah, 213).
short_answer: 3 groups: 1. Paradise (good outweighs). 2. A'raf (equal). 3. Hell (sins outweigh, but will exit).
source: Al-Anbiya, 47; Al-A'raf, 8-9, 46-49; Az-Zalzalah, 6-8; Hadiths (Bukhari, Muslim, Haythami)

question: Does the application of Sharia-prescribed punishments for various transgressions serve as expiation for these transgressions?
answer: It is reported that once the Prophet ﷺ, surrounded by his companions, said: 'Pledge allegiance to me that you will not associate anything with Allah, will not steal, will not commit adultery, will not kill your children, will not spread falsehood fabricated by your hearts, and will not act contrary to what is approved by Sharia. Whoever among you is faithful to this oath, Allah will reward him, and whoever violates it in something and is punished in this world, this will serve as expiation for his sin. But if someone violates it in something and Allah conceals it, then Allah will decide his fate - if He wills, He will forgive him, and if He wills, He will punish him.' Ubadah said: 'And we pledged allegiance to him in this.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim).
short_answer: Yes, punishment in this world (hadd) is expiation (kaffarah).

question: How can one reconcile the words of the Prophet ﷺ quoted in the aforementioned hadith, who said: '...then Allah will decide his fate - if He wills, He will forgive him, and if He wills, He will punish him,' with the words that a person whose bad deeds outweigh the good will enter the Fire, as mentioned earlier?
answer: There is no contradiction between one and the other, for if Allah wishes to forgive such a person, He will not demand a detailed account from him, the interpretation of which was given by the Prophet ﷺ, who said that this can happen during the presentation of deeds for Judgment. And about this he ﷺ also said: 'Each of you will draw near to his Lord so that He will cover him and say: "Did you do such-and-such?" and he will say: "Yes." And He will say: "Did you do such-and-such?" and he will say: "Yes," confirming this, and then He will say: "Indeed, I covered you in earthly life, and today I forgive you!"' (Al-Bukhari). As for those who will enter the Fire for their sins, they will be people who will be subjected to a serious reckoning, about whom the Prophet ﷺ said: 'And those from whom a detailed account is demanded will be subjected to torments.' (Al-Bukhari, At-Tirmidhi, Ahmad).
short_answer: Forgiveness is 'easy reckoning.' Punishment is 'detailed account' (munaqashah).

question: What specifically is meant by the straight path (as-sirat al-mustaqim), which Allah commanded us to follow while forbidding us to follow other paths?
answer: This refers to the religion called Islam, with which Allah sent His messengers to people and which is mentioned in the Scriptures He revealed. Nothing other than this religion will be accepted from anyone, and no one will be saved except those who follow this path. For one who does not follow this path, paths will branch out and lead him astray. Allah the Almighty said: 'And indeed, this is My straight path, so follow it; and do not follow other ways, for they will separate you from His way.' (Al-An'am, 153). As for the Prophet ﷺ, it is reported that once he drew a straight line on the ground, then said: 'This is the straight path of Allah.' Then he drew many lines to the right and left of this line and said: 'And among these paths there is not one where there is no devil calling to it,' - after which he recited this verse: 'And indeed, this is My straight path, so follow it; and do not follow other ways, for they will separate you from His way.' (Al-An'am, 153; Ahmad, Al-Hakim). It is also reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Allah used the straight path as an example. On both sides of this path are fences with open doors, and on the doors are lowered curtains. At the gate leading to this path is a caller who says: "O people, enter the straight path all together and do not divide!" Another caller addresses people while positioned above this path, and if a person wants to open any of the doors, he says: "Woe to you, do not open this door, for if you open it, you will enter it!" This straight path is Islam, the fences are the commandments of Allah, the open doors are what Allah has forbidden, the caller at the beginning of the path is the Book of Allah, and the caller who is above this path is the admonisher of Allah, which is in the heart of every Muslim.' (Ahmad, Al-Hakim).
short_answer: Islam, the Quran and Sunnah.

question: What allows one to follow the straight path and avoid deviations from it?
answer: This is achieved only through adherence to the Quran and Sunnah, when a person moves with them and stops at the boundaries they establish. This is precisely what allows one to adhere to pure Tawhid and properly follow the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, for Allah the Almighty said: 'And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger will be with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor - of the prophets, the steadfast, the martyrs and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions!' (An-Nisa, 69). The people favored by Allah and mentioned in this verse are the same people referred to as guided on the straight path in the first surah of the Quran. Allah the Almighty said: '...Guide us to the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, not of those who have evoked Your anger or of those who are astray.' (Al-Fatihah, 6-7). And there is no greater blessing for a servant of Allah than being guided to this straight path and removed from the paths of misguidance. In such a state the Prophet ﷺ left his ummah, about which he himself said: 'I have left you upon a clear path, from which after me none will deviate except the utterly doomed.' (Ahmad, Ibn Majah, Al-Hakim).
short_answer: Following the Quran and Sunnah.
source: An-Nisa, 69; Al-Fatihah, 6-7; Hadiths (Ahmad, Ibn Majah, Hakim)

question: What is the opposite of the Sunnah?
answer: Its opposite is innovations (bid'ah) invented by people, in other words, imposing as obligatory what Allah did not permit. This is precisely what the Prophet ﷺ meant when he said: 'If anyone introduces into this matter of ours that which does not belong to it, it will be rejected.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). And the Prophet ﷺ also said: 'You must adhere to my Sunnah and the Sunnah of the rightly-guided caliphs. Hold firmly to it and beware of newly-invented matters, for every innovation is misguidance!' (Ahmad, Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah). And the Prophet ﷺ indicated that such deviations will inevitably occur in the future, also indicating who will avoid them, as stated in the following hadith: It is reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'My ummah will split into seventy-three groups: all of them will be in the Fire except one.' People asked: 'Who will be in this group, O Messenger of Allah?' 'Those who follow what I and my Companions follow.' (Al-Hakim, At-Tirmidhi). And Allah the Almighty separated the Prophet ﷺ from those who adhere to innovations, saying: 'Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects - you have nothing to do with them. Their affair is only to Allah...' (Al-An'am, 159).
short_answer: Bid'ah (Innovation).
source: Hadiths (Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi); Al-An'am, 159

question: How should one regard the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and members of his family?
answer: What is obligatory for us is to be sincere toward them and not say anything bad about them, tell people about their virtues, refrain from mentioning their shortcomings and the contradictions that arose between them, and mention them only as the Most High mentioned these people in the Torah, the Gospel and the Quran, and in accordance with what is said about their virtues in authentic hadiths and other well-known sources. Allah the Almighty said: 'Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and His pleasure. Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration. That is their description in the Torah. And their description in the Gospel is as a plant which produces its offshoots and strengthens them so they grow firm and stand upon their stalks, delighting the sowers - so that He may enrage by them the disbelievers. Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds among them forgiveness and a great reward.' (Al-Fath, 29). 'And those who believed, emigrated and fought in the cause of Allah, and those who gave shelter and aided - they are the true believers. For them is forgiveness and noble provision.' (Al-Anfal, 74). 'And the first forerunners among the Muhajirun and the Ansar and those who followed them with good conduct - Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him, and He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. That is the great attainment.' (At-Tawbah, 100). 'Allah has already forgiven the Prophet and the Muhajirun and the Ansar who followed him in the hour of difficulty...' (At-Tawbah, 117). 'And there is a share for the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their properties, seeking bounty from Allah and His approval and supporting Allah and His Messenger. Those are the truthful. And those who were settled in the home and adopted the faith before them. They love those who emigrated to them and find not any want in their breasts of what they were given but give them preference over themselves, even though they are in privation.' (Al-Hashr, 8-9). And we know and believe that Allah the Almighty looked upon the participants in the Battle of Badr and said: 'Do what you will, for I have already forgiven you.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim) - and there were more than three hundred and ten of them. And we believe that none of those who gave the pledge under the tree will enter the Fire, and that Allah is pleased with them as they are pleased with Allah, and there were one thousand four hundred of them, while some say there were one and a half thousand, for Allah the Almighty said: 'Certainly was Allah pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree. He knew what was in their hearts...' (Al-Fath, 18). And we testify that they constituted the best generation of this ummah, which is the best of religious communities, and that if any of those who come after them spends a mountain of gold the size of Mount Uhud, it will not equal any of them if he spent even one mudd or even half a mudd. And although we believe they were not protected from sins and could make mistakes, they strove in search of truth, and for their efforts, the one among them who succeeded deserves double reward, while the one who erred deserves one, and their mistakes are forgiven. And they possessed such virtues and performed so many righteous deeds that this removed all evil they committed, if they committed any evil at all. Can a small amount of something impure change an entire sea if it ends up in it? May Allah be pleased with them and make them pleased! And we can say the same about the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, who were members of his family, whom Allah relieved from all impurity and purified completely. And we have nothing in common with those who think badly or say anything bad about the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and members of his family in general or about any of them individually, and we call upon Allah the Almighty as witness that we love them, support them and defend them to the best of our ability, following the testament of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: 'Do not revile my Companions.' And the Prophet ﷺ also said: 'Fear Allah, fear Allah regarding my Companions! Fear Allah, fear Allah regarding my Companions! Do not make them objects of attack after me, for whoever loves them loves them because he loves me, and whoever hates them hates them because he hates me!' (At-Tirmidhi, Ahmad). It is also reported that once the Prophet ﷺ said: 'And I leave among you two precious things. The first of them is the Book of Allah, which contains guidance and light, so take the Book of Allah and hold firmly to it!' - and he began to urge people to adhere to the Book of Allah - 'The second precious thing is my family' - and after this the Prophet ﷺ repeated three times: '...and I remind you of the need to fear Allah regarding my family.' (Muslim, Ahmad, Al-Hakim). Other hadiths could also be cited as examples.
short_answer: Love, respect, do not discuss their mistakes.
source: Al-Fath, 18, 29; Al-Anfal, 74; At-Tawbah, 100, 117; Al-Hashr, 8-9; Hadiths (Bukhari, Muslim, Tirmidhi, Ahmad, Hakim)

question: Who among the Companions in general was the most virtuous?
answer: The most virtuous are the first forerunners among the Muhajirun and Ansar, then the participants in the Battle of Badr, then the participants in the Battle of Uhud, then the people who gave the pledge pleasing to Allah, and then all the rest. And Allah the Almighty said: 'Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest. Those are greater in degree than those who spent afterwards and fought. But to all Allah has promised the best reward.' (Al-Hadid, 10).
short_answer: Muhajirun and Ansar (the forerunners), the Badrians.

question: Who specifically among the Companions was the most virtuous?
answer: It is reported that Abdullah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: 'During the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ, we did not equate anyone with Abu Bakr, then with Umar, then with Uthman, after which we no longer gave preference to any of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ over others.' (Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi). It is also reported that in the cave the Prophet ﷺ said to Abu Bakr: 'What do you think of two, the third of whom is Allah?' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is also reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'If I were to choose a beloved friend (khalil), I would choose Abu Bakr, but he is my brother and companion.' It is also reported that once the Prophet ﷺ said twice: 'Indeed, Allah sent me to you, and you said: "You lied," but Abu Bakr said: "You spoke the truth," and he helped me both personally and with his wealth, so will you not leave my companion alone?' (Al-Bukhari). It is also reported that once the Prophet ﷺ said: 'O Ibn al-Khattab, by Him in whose hand is my soul, if the devil meets you somewhere on the road, he will certainly choose another road for himself.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is also reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Among those who lived before you, there were already those who received inspiration from above, and if there is one such person in my ummah, then truly, it is Umar.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is also reported that once, after telling people about a conversation between a wolf and a cow, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Indeed, I believe in this, and Abu Bakr and Umar believe, who were not there.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is reported that during the pledge of allegiance pleasing to Allah, when Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him) went to Mecca, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a sign with his right hand, wanting to say that this was Uthman's hand, then struck it against his other hand and said: 'This is for Uthman.' (Al-Bukhari, At-Tirmidhi). It is also reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'For the one who digs the well of Rumah, Paradise will be the reward' - and Uthman dug it. (Al-Bukhari). It is also reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'For the one who equipped the army in the difficult campaign, Paradise will be the reward' - and one of those who equipped it was Uthman. It is also reported that about Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him), the Prophet ﷺ said: 'How can I not be ashamed of one whom the angels are ashamed of?!' (Muslim, Al-Hakim). It is also reported that once the Prophet ﷺ said to Ali (may Allah be pleased with him): 'You are to me and I am to you.' (Al-Bukhari, At-Tirmidhi, Ahmad). And the Prophet ﷺ announced that Ali loves Allah and His Messenger, and Allah and His Messenger love him. (Muslim, At-Tirmidhi). It is also reported that once the Prophet ﷺ said to Ali (may Allah be pleased with him): 'Are you not content to be to me as Harun was to Musa, except that there will be no prophet after me?' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is narrated from Sa'id ibn Zayd (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Ten people will be in Paradise: the Prophet ﷺ will be in Paradise, and Abu Bakr will be in Paradise, and Umar will be in Paradise, and Uthman will be in Paradise, and Ali will be in Paradise, and Talhah will be in Paradise, and Az-Zubayr ibn Al-Awwam will be in Paradise, and Sa'd ibn Malik will be in Paradise, and Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf will be in Paradise' - and if you wish, I will name the tenth. People asked: 'Who is he?' but he remained silent. People asked again: 'Who is he?' He said: 'It is Sa'id ibn Zayd.' (Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi). It is also reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'The most merciful of my ummah toward its members is Abu Bakr, the most steadfast of them in the religion of Allah is Umar, the most modest is Uthman, the most knowledgeable about rulings concerning inheritance is Zayd ibn Thabit, the best reciter of the Book of Allah is Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and the best knower of the lawful and unlawful is Mu'adh ibn Jabal. And every ummah has its trustee (amin), and the trustee of this ummah is Abu Ubaydah ibn Al-Jarrah.' (Ahmad, At-Tirmidhi, Al-Hakim). It is also reported that about Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn will be the masters of the youth of Paradise.' (At-Tirmidhi, Al-Hakim). And he ﷺ said: 'They are my two sweet basils in this world.' (Al-Bukhari, At-Tirmidhi). It is also reported that about them the Prophet ﷺ said: 'O Allah, I love them, so love them too!' (Al-Bukhari, At-Tirmidhi). It is also reported that about Al-Hasan the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Indeed, this son of mine will be a master, and perhaps through him Allah will reconcile two great groups of Muslims' - which indeed happened later. (Al-Bukhari, At-Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud, Ahmad). It is also reported that about their mother the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Fatimah will be the mistress of the women of Paradise.' (Al-Bukhari, At-Tirmidhi). And in many other hadiths it is reported about the numerous virtues of the Companions in general and their individual representatives, however, an indication that one of them possessed a particular virtue does not yet mean that they surpassed others in this, and this applies to all except the four rightly-guided caliphs. Such a conclusion regarding the first three of them can be made based on the aforementioned hadith transmitted from Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both). As for Ali, by unanimous opinion of the members of the Muslim ummah, after them he was the most virtuous of those living on earth.
short_answer: Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, as well as the others from the 10 promised Paradise.
source: Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi, Bukhari, Muslim, Ahmad, Hakim

question: How long did the caliphate exist after the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?
answer: It is reported that Safinah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The prophetic caliphate will exist for thirty years, and then Allah will give power to whom He wills."' (Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi, Ahmad, Al-Hakim). And the caliphate during which Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali (may Allah be pleased with them) ruled indeed existed for exactly that much time, with Abu Bakr being caliph for two years and three months, Umar for ten years and six months, Uthman for twelve years, and Ali for four years and nine months, which, including the rule of Al-Hasan ibn Ali for six months, makes exactly thirty years. The founder of the first ruling dynasty was Mu'awiyah (may Allah be pleased with him), who was the best and most virtuous of them, after whom came a period of unjust rule that continued until power passed to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz (may Allah be pleased with him). Adherents of the Sunnah even consider him the fifth rightly-guided caliph, since he followed the example of the first four.
short_answer: 30 years (Rightly-Guided Caliphate).

question: What can serve as an indication that these four were indeed rightly-guided caliphs?
answer: There are a great many such indications. Among them is the limitation of the caliphate to thirty years, which corresponded to the time of their rule. Among them is also the preference for them over others, which was mentioned earlier, as well as their superiority over one another, which corresponded to the order of their rule. The most convincing indication of this is the unanimous recognition of them as rightly-guided caliphs by authoritative figures, which no one objects to except the misguided and adherents of innovations.
short_answer: Coincidence of the 30-year term and Ijma (consensus) of the ummah.

question: What indications exist that the first three of them were indeed rightly-guided caliphs?
answer: There are many such indications. Among them are those we have already cited, as well as the hadith transmitted from Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), who reported that once the Prophet ﷺ asked: 'Who among you saw a dream?' One man said: 'I saw that scales were lowered from the sky, on which you and Abu Bakr were weighed, and you outweighed Abu Bakr, and Umar and Abu Bakr were weighed, and Abu Bakr outweighed, and Umar and Uthman were weighed, and Umar outweighed, and then these scales were raised.' (Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi, Al-Hakim).
short_answer: The hadith about scales (dream), which shows the order of their virtue.

question: What in general can be said about Abu Bakr and Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) being rightly-guided caliphs?
answer: There are many indications of this. A well-known hadith reports that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'In a dream I saw myself at a well, on the edge of which stood a bucket, and I drew from this well as much water as Allah willed. Then Ibn Abi Quhafah took this bucket and drew one or two buckets from there, and then, doing this, he showed weakness, and Allah forgave him his weakness. Then this bucket turned into a huge leather bucket, and Ibn al-Khattab took it, and I did not see any leader among people draw as Umar did, and this continued until people drove their livestock to rest.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim).
short_answer: The Prophet's dream about the well and buckets.

question: What indicates that Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) rightfully became the first caliph?
answer: There are a great many such indications. Some of them have already been cited by us. Among them is also the hadith in which it is reported that once a woman came to the Prophet ﷺ, to whom he told her to return again. She asked: 'Tell me, what if I come but don't find you?' - as if meaning that he might die. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'If you don't find me, turn to Abu Bakr.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is also reported that Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: 'Once the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "Call your father and your brother to me so I can write a will, for I fear that there will be those who desire and someone will say: 'I am more worthy,' - whereas Allah and the believers want no one but Abu Bakr."' (Muslim). And the same thing the Prophet ﷺ said when appointing Abu Bakr as imam for prayer when he himself fell ill shortly before his death. Moreover, allegiance to Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) was given by all the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from among the Muhajirun and Ansar, as well as other people.
short_answer: Direct indications of the Prophet and unanimous pledge (ijma) of the Companions.

question: What indications are there that after Abu Bakr, Umar should rightfully have become caliph?
answer: There are many such indications, and some of them have already been cited by us earlier. Among them is that once the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Indeed, I do not know how much longer I will remain among you, so follow the example of those who will be after me' - and saying this, he pointed to Abu Bakr and Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both). (At-Tirmidhi, Ahmad, Al-Hakim). And among such indications is the content of the hadith that speaks of a tribulation that will rage like the sea. This hadith reports that Hudhayfah (may Allah be pleased with him) said to Umar: 'Indeed, a locked door separates you from this tribulation.' Umar asked: 'Will it be opened or broken?' He answered: 'Only broken' - after which Umar said: 'Then it will never close.' This door was Umar himself, and to break it meant to kill Umar. And after him, tribulations in the Muslim ummah never ceased. (Al-Bukhari, Muslim - part of a long hadith). And all members of the Muslim ummah came to the unanimous opinion that after Abu Bakr, Umar should have become caliph (may Allah be pleased with them both).
short_answer: The command to follow him and the hadith about the 'door' from fitnah.

question: What indications are there that after Abu Bakr and Umar, Uthman should rightfully have become caliph?
answer: There are many such indications, and some of them have already been cited by us earlier. Among them is also the hadith transmitted from Ka'b ibn Ujrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: 'Once the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned an inevitable coming tribulation. At that time, some man with a covered head was passing by, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "At that time, this man will adhere to the right path." Then I rushed forward, grabbed Uthman by the hands, then turned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked: "This one?" - and he said: "This one."' (At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Ahmad, Al-Hakim). It is reported that Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: 'Once the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said three times: "O Uthman, if Allah ever entrusts you with power over this, and the hypocrites wish that you take off that shirt which Allah will put on you, do not take it off!"' (At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Ahmad). And all members of the council (shura) agreed that allegiance should be given to him, and then all other Companions joined them, with the first to pledge allegiance to him after Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf being Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), and then all other people pledged allegiance to him.
short_answer: The hadith about the 'shirt' (power) from Allah and the choice of the council (Shura).

question: What indications are there that after them, Ali had preferential right to the caliphate?
answer: There are many such indications, and some of them have already been cited by us earlier. Among them is also the report that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Woe to Ammar, for he will be killed by a group of wrongdoers whom he will be calling to Paradise, while they will be calling him to Hell.' (Al-Bukhari, Ahmad). And indeed, Ammar was with Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both) when he was killed by the people of Sham, whom he was calling to the Sunnah, agreement and obedience to the true leader, that is, Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him). It is also reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'During a split among people, apostates will apostatize, and the one of the two groups that is closer to the truth will kill them.' (Muslim, Ahmad). And indeed, the Khawarij became apostates, and Ali fought them in the Battle of Nahrawan, and he was closer to the truth, by unanimous opinion of all adherents of the Sunnah - may Allah the Almighty have mercy on all of them.
short_answer: The hadiths about Ammar and the Khawarij confirm Ali's righteousness.

question: Who has the obligation to enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil, and what levels of this exist?
answer: Allah the Almighty and Great said: 'And let there be among you a nation inviting to good, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. Those are the successful.' (Al Imran, 104). As for the Prophet ﷺ, it is reported that he said: 'Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he is unable, then with his tongue; if he is unable, then with his heart - and that is the weakest of faith.' (Muslim). Many other Quranic verses and hadiths speak of this, and all of them indicate that enjoining good and attempting to forbid evil are the duty of everyone who sees that this is necessary. No one is exempt from this unless someone else has already done it, and the greater the capabilities and knowledge a servant of Allah possesses, the more obligatory this becomes for him. When sinners are subjected to torments, no one will be saved except those who tried to restrain people from sins.
short_answer: Upon everyone according to their ability (by hand, word, heart).

question: What can be said about the miracles of people close to Allah (karamat al-awliya)?
answer: Such miracles can indeed occur. These are supernatural things related to them, which, however, are not performed by them themselves and to which they themselves do not aspire. All this is performed through them by Allah, even if they do not know about it. Examples include the story of the youths of the cave, the story of the people who were covered by a rock fragment, and the story of Jurayj - and all these miracles were related to the miracles of their prophets. This is why the greatest number of the greatest miracles were performed in this ummah: this is explained by the greatness of the miracles of its Prophet and the degree to which this Prophet was honored by Allah the Almighty and Great. Reports are known about what happened with Abu Bakr during the period of apostasy (riddah), about how Umar, standing on the minbar of the mosque in Medina, addressed Sariyah, who was at that time in Sham, and these words were heard by him, and about how he wrote a letter to the Nile, about how during the conquest of Rum, Al-Ala ibn Al-Hadrami directed his horse into the sea and it walked on water, about how Abu Muslim Al-Khawlani prayed in the fire that Al-Aswad Al-Ansi kindled for him, and about many other events of this kind that took place with Muslims both during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ and during the times of the Companions and those who followed them with pure hearts, which occurred subsequently, up to our days, and will still occur until the very Day of Resurrection. And all this in essence is nothing other than miracles of our Prophet ﷺ, since they received the ability to perform such things only through following him. If something supernatural is performed by a person who is not a follower of this Prophet, then this is not a miracle but a trial and deception, and such a person belongs not to those close to the Merciful, but to the devils - may Allah protect us from this!
short_answer: Karamat are real, occur by Allah's will and confirm prophethood.

question: Who are counted among those close (awliya) to Allah?
answer: Among those close is every one of those who believed in Allah, began to fear Him and followed His Messenger ﷺ. Allah the Almighty said: 'Indeed, the close servants of Allah have nothing to fear, nor shall they grieve.' (Yunus, 62). And then He explained who belongs to their number, saying: 'Those who believed and were God-fearing...' (Yunus, 63). 'Allah is the Protector of those who believe. He brings them out from darkness into light. As for those who disbelieve, their protectors are taghut. They bring them out from light into darkness.' (Al-Baqarah, 257). Allah the Almighty also said: 'Your protector is only Allah, and His Messenger and those who believe, who establish prayer and give zakah and bow down. And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as protectors - they are the party of Allah, and they will be victorious.' (Al-Ma'idah, 55-56). As for the Prophet ﷺ, it is reported that he said: 'Indeed, the family of so-and-so are not my protectors; my protectors are only Allah and righteous believers.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is reported that Al-Hasan Al-Basri (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Allah tested people who claim their love for Allah, saying: "Say, 'If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you..."' (Al Imran, 31). It is reported that Imam Ash-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'If you see a person who walks on water or flies through the air, do not believe him and do not be seduced by him until you are convinced that he is a follower of the Messenger ﷺ!'
short_answer: Every God-fearing believer.

question: Which group did the Prophet ﷺ mean when he said: 'A group of people from my ummah will continue to adhere manifestly to the truth, and those who oppose them will not harm them until the command of Allah the Almighty comes'?
answer: This group is one of the seventy-three groups and the only one that will be saved, as the Prophet ﷺ indicated, saying: 'All of them will be in the Fire except one, and this is the people of unity (al-jama'ah).' (Ibn Majah, Ahmad). In another version of this hadith it is reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: '...and these are those who will adhere to what I and my Companions adhere to today.' (At-Tirmidhi, Al-Hakim). We ask Allah the Almighty to count us among these people, and not to lead our hearts astray after He has guided us to it, and to grant us mercy from Himself, for indeed, He is the Bestower. 'Exalted is your Lord, Lord of might, above what they describe. And peace upon the messengers. And praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds!' (As-Saffat, 180-182).
short_answer: Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah (those who follow the Prophet and the Companions).
source: Bukhari, Muslim, Ibn Majah, Ahmad, Tirmidhi, Hakim
